_note: Lane-cited dictionary entries — standard classical Arabic meanings for high-frequency JA tokens in Saadia's Tafsir. Hand-curated against the corpus; not auto-generated. `source: "lane"` means "this is the standard classical Arabic sense, for which Lane's Lexicon is the canonical English reference" — entries paraphrase, they are not verbatim Lane quotes. For Saadia-specific or Blau-divergent senses, see data/tafsir-divergence.json. For tribute and Blau-citation policy, see /about/blau.
_source: Lane's Lexicon (E.W. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, 1863-1893; public domain). Roots verified against the Perseus TEI edition at ~/Tools/arabic-lexicon/lane-xml.
_scope: Hand-curated 2026-05-21; first batch ≈70 entries focused on top-frequency tokens from the Bereshit-Devarim corpus that are NOT in tafsir-divergence.json. Inflected surface forms (suffixed prepositions, fa-prefixed perfects) included where they appear ≥100x in the corpus to improve tap-to-define UX without yet extending the prefix/suffix-stripping logic in lib/lookup.ts.

entries.saadia_note: Saadia's divine-name rendering, esp. paired with אלכאפי for Hebrew אֵל שַׁדַּי. Component of Saadia's compound divine name 'אלטאיק אלכאפי' (the All-Capable, the Sufficient) — his rendering of Hebrew אֵל שַׁדַּי. See the divergence cards on Bereshit 17 for context.
Saadia's divine-name rendering — see טאיק.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew מֵעַל and עַל in 'over/above' senses.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew נְחֹשֶׁת.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew נָדִיב and נִכְבָּד.

entries.notes: Broken plural of שריף. Add as standalone lemma so the bare form resolves outside the divergence-card flow.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים in Gen 6 — the 'sons of the noble class'. Already discussed under tafsir-divergence (Gen 6:2, 6:4: 'sons-of-the-nobility' for בני האלהים).

entries.notes: Form VIII (reflexive-derived) of خ-ي-ر 'good/excellent' → 'to pick the best'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew בָּחַר. See the divergence card for אכ'תיאר (Gen 4:7) for the noun/abstract form.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew קָרָא in 'call' and 'read' senses. Direct Saadia rendering of Hebrew קָרָא — the cognate carries over.

entries.notes: Heavy in Exodus 27-38.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew קֶלַע — the courtyard hangings of the Tabernacle. Persian-origin loanword in Arabic, used by Saadia for the screen-fabric panels of the Tabernacle courtyard.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew שִׁטִּים — the wood of the Tabernacle.

entries.gloss_en: weight; weighing; (as verb wazana) he weighed-out
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew שָׁקַל and מִשְׁקָל.

entries.gloss_en: the (definite article); (as standalone) the article in isolation, typically a citation form or break in text
entries.notes: Normally proclitic: prefixes onto a noun. The standalone form is rare and usually a citation or text break.
Denominative imperfect built on the adjective נגס 'unclean' (see the נגס entry). High-frequency in Vayikra purity laws.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's denominative of nájisun 'unclean'.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew מָצָא.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew תּוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי — the scarlet/crimson tabernacle thread.

entries.notes: Persian asmān 'sky' + gūn 'color' → 'sky-colored'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew תְּכֵלֶת. Saadia's signature rendering of the tabernacle's blue thread.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew הָרַג and הִכָּה לְמָוֶת.

entries.gloss_en: time, point-in-time, appointed-moment; (broken pl. awqāt) times
entries.notes: The bare singular waqt — companion to the existing אוקאת (the broken plural).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses both.

entries.notes: Compound of demonstrative ها 'behold' + 1sg pronoun אנא.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew הִנֵּנִי and הִנֵּה אֲנִי. Saadia's rendering of Hebrew הִנֵּנִי.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew סָפַר, פָּקַד, נָשָׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ in census contexts.

entries.gloss_en: petty chief, lesser leader (diminutive of raʾīs)
entries.notes: Diminutive of رئيس 'chief'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's nuanced rendering of secondary tribal-leadership terms. Saadia uses this form to differentiate junior leadership (e.g. heads of sub-clans) from the principal נשיא.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew עָנָן.
in Saadia — used for circumcision-covenant community contexts. Saadia uses millah (and its derivatives) in contexts of religious-community identity; appears in covenant-circumcision narratives.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אָכַל.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אֹכֶל.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew טָהוֹר.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew רָם and גָּבוֹהַּ.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew רָצוֹן and לְרָצוֹן in offering contexts.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew כֵּלִים in cultic-utensil contexts.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew עַתּוּד — Hebrew form retained.

Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אֲדוֹנִי in human-respect contexts; NOT for the divine Name. Saadia uses סייד for human masters and respected superiors (e.g. אדני in interpersonal contexts). For the divine Name יהוה Saadia uses אללה.
Saadia's divine-name rendering in some contexts; mostly an epithet. An Arabic divine epithet (also in the Qurʾan, Surat al-Ikhlāṣ); Saadia uses it sparingly in his theological prose.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew יְאֹר and פִּישׁוֹן. Geographic identification long established in Saadia: יְאֹר (and elsewhere פִּישׁוֹן) = the Nile.

entries.notes: Form IV (causative) of qāma 'to stand'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew הֵקִים. Saadia's regular rendering of the Hebrew hiphil הֵקִים.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew נָשִׂיא.

entries.gloss_en: Lot (Abraham's nephew; father of Moab and Ammon)
Abimelech (king of Gerar / Philistia in Gen 20-21, 26)
Rebecca (Isaac's wife; mother of Jacob and Esau)
Nun (father of Joshua, of the tribe of Ephraim)
Joshua (son of Nun; Moses' attendant and successor)
Gershon (firstborn of Levi; the Gershonite clan)
Kohath (second son of Levi; ancestor of Moses, Aaron, Miriam)
Hagar (Sarah's Egyptian handmaid; mother of Ishmael)
Cain (firstborn of Adam; killer of Abel)
entries.notes: Homograph with the Kenite tribal gentilic — context disambiguates.

entries.gloss_en: Abel (second son of Adam, killed by Cain)
Dinah (daughter of Jacob and Leah; Gen 30, 34)
Ephron the Hittite (seller of the Machpelah cave; Gen 23)
Ishmael (son of Abraham and Hagar; ancestor of the Arab nations)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses the Arabic form אסמאעיל (Ismāʿīl) throughout the Tafsir for Hebrew יִשְׁמָעֵאל. The Arabic surface form makes the cross-tradition lineage explicit.

entries.gloss_en: Sihon (Amorite king of Heshbon; Num 21, Deut 2-3)
Aram (the Aramaean region of upper Mesopotamia / Syria)
Midian (descendant of Abraham via Keturah; the Midianite people)
Arnon (river forming the southern border of trans-Jordanian Israel)
Jabbok (river east of the Jordan; site of Jacob's wrestling, Gen 32)
Jericho (the lowland city west of the Jordan)
the Red Sea — al-Qulzum, the medieval Arabic name for Hebrew יַם סוּף
entries.notes: Medieval Arabic geographers used al-Qulzum (Clysma, near modern Suez) as the standard name for the entire Red Sea / Gulf of Suez.

entries.gloss_en: Goshen — al-Sadir, the medieval Arabic identification of the Egyptian region where Israel dwelt (Hebrew גֹּשֶׁן)
Gerar — al-Khalus, the medieval Arabic identification of the Philistine city in the western Negev (Hebrew גְּרָר)
the Euphrates — al-Furāt, the standard Arabic name for Hebrew פְּרָת
Mosul — al-Mawṣil, the medieval Arabic identification of biblical אַשּׁוּר (Asshur, region/city in upper Mesopotamia)
Nablus — the medieval Arabic identification of biblical שְׁכֶם (Shechem, the Samaritan city)
Abyssinia / Ethiopia — al-Ḥabash, the medieval Arabic identification of biblical כּוּשׁ (Cush)
Zawila — the medieval Arabic identification of biblical חֲוִילָה (Havilah, the gold-bearing land of Gen 2:11)
Banyas — the medieval Arabic identification of the city of Dan at the headwaters of the Jordan
the Tigris — Dijla, the standard Arabic name for Hebrew חִדֶּקֶל
Qardū — the medieval Arabic/Aramaic identification of biblical אֲרָרָט (Ararat), the mountain range in northern Mesopotamia where Noah's ark rested
entries.notes: Matches the Targum Onqelos rendering and Q11:44.

entries.gloss_en: he begot, fathered; (fem.) she gave birth, bore
entries.notes: Form I walada/yalidu. Distinct from the noun ولد 'child' (same surface form, same root, separate entry).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's standard rendering of Hebrew יָלַד / הוֹלִיד throughout the patriarchal genealogies.

entries.gloss_en: he/it became, came to be, turned into
entries.notes: Verb of becoming; takes its predicate in the accusative. Frequent in narrative continuations.
entries.saadia_note: A workhorse linker in Saadia's narrative prose, often glossing the Hebrew וַיְהִי 'and it came to be'.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew שָׁמַע — both physical hearing and obedient heeding (וְשָׁמַעְתָּ בְּקוֹלוֹ).
One of Saadia's renderings for Hebrew שָׁלַח (also covered by ארסל), often used for divine commissioning.

entries.gloss_en: he did, made, performed, acted; worked
entries.notes: Active verb of doing; the masdar עמל also means 'work, deed'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's primary gloss for Hebrew עָשָׂה (general action) — contrast צנע (skilled craft) and געל (set/place).

entries.gloss_en: he drew near, approached, came close
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew קָרַב (drew near). The Form IV אקרב 'to bring near' is the standard rendering of הִקְרִיב (offered up).
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew חָיָה in the genealogies — 'and he lived N years and begot…'.
Saadia's standard gloss for Hebrew בּוֹא (came). Often paired with אתי 'arrived/brought'.
Saadia uses the active participle ואקף for Hebrew עוֹמֵד ('standing'), especially in court/courtier contexts.

entries.gloss_en: he accepted, received; (Form IV) he approached, came toward
entries.notes: Form I قَبِلَ 'to accept'; Form IV أَقْبَلَ 'to come toward, approach'. The surface form אקבל is homographous between Form-I 1s-imperfect ('I accept') and Form-IV 3ms-perfect ('he approached').
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses Form IV אקבל heavily for Hebrew פָּנָה (turned toward).

entries.gloss_en: he released, set loose, declared; let go
entries.notes: Form IV of طلق. Also bears the technical sense 'to use a term unrestrictedly / absolutely' in kalām and grammar.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses אטלק for Hebrew שִׁלַּח 'sent away, released' in the freeing-the-slave passages.

entries.gloss_en: he came, arrived; (with object) he brought
entries.notes: Final-yāʾ weak verb. The Form IV ātā 'to give, bring to' has the surface form אאתי (sometimes spelled אתי).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's frequent gloss for Hebrew בּוֹא alongside גא; the jussive יאת (with optional li-) renders Hebrew יָבוֹא in commands.

entries.gloss_en: it intensified, grew severe, became strong
entries.notes: Form VIII reflexive of shadd 'to be hard/strong'. The Form I shadda and Form IV ashadda are also frequent.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses אשתד for Hebrew כָּבֵד (was heavy/severe) — esp. in the plague narratives (וַיֶּחֱזַק / וַיִּכְבַּד).

entries.notes: Hollow verb fāḍa/yafīḍu. Common in poetic and exegetical registers for abundance.

entries.gloss_en: births, progeny, generations (broken pl. of mawlūd / tilād)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's standing rendering of Hebrew תּוֹלְדוֹת (generations, lineage).
Saadia's standard gloss for Hebrew זֶרַע 'seed/offspring' in the patriarchal blessings.
Saadia uses ג'ריב for Hebrew גֵּר (sojourner) in the welfare-of-the-stranger commandments.

entries.gloss_en: base, foundation, pillar, footing; (broken pl.) qawāʿid — bases, supports
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's term for the bases (אֲדָנִים) of the tabernacle uprights, esp. in Exodus 26–27 and 36–38.

entries.gloss_en: purple, purple-dyed wool/cloth (a costly violet-red dye)
entries.notes: Loanword shared with Hebrew אַרְגָּמָן and Aramaic ארגוון. Designates both the dye and the cloth dyed with it.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's standard rendering of Hebrew אַרְגָּמָן in the tabernacle and priestly-vestments passages.

entries.gloss_en: twisted, twined (esp. of thread or linen plied for fine weaving)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's rendering of Hebrew מָשְׁזָר 'twisted (linen)' in the tabernacle and priestly-vestments specifications.

entries.gloss_en: lord, master, protector, patron; (with pron.) my Lord
entries.notes: Vocative מולאי 'O my Lord' is common in petitionary speech. Broken plural: mawālī (מואלי).
entries.saadia_note: One of Saadia's reverential forms of address in the patriarchal dialogues with God; in human contexts it renders Hebrew אֲדוֹנִי.

entries.gloss_en: he drew near, came close, approached
entries.notes: Form I dana/yadnū. Frequent in legal/cultic passages re: physical proximity (esp. to a corpse, to holy things).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses דנא alongside קרב for Hebrew קָרַב / נָגַשׁ — the contact-impurity passages in Numbers 19 use דנא heavily.

entries.gloss_en: this; (with li-) such; (in oaths) this same one
entries.notes: Bare demonstrative ذا (the source of هذا 'this' and ذلك 'that'). Appears stand-alone in idioms and after particles.

entries.gloss_en: favor, share, portion, good fortune (a lot allotted to one)
entries.notes: Verbal noun of حظي 'to enjoy favor / receive a share'. The form حظوة is the feminine masdar; حظا is the indefinite accusative.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's standing gloss for Hebrew חֵן 'favor' in the patriarchal narratives — 'finding favor in someone's eyes'.

entries.gloss_en: he went, passed, proceeded; (of time) elapsed
entries.notes: Final-yāʾ weak verb. The imperative امضِ ('go!') has the JA surface form אמץ' or אמץ.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's frequent gloss for Hebrew קוּם לֵךְ — 'arise, go' is rendered as קום אמץ'. Saadia uses it both for physical motion and the passing of time.

entries.gloss_en: special, particular, choice; (broken pl. khawāṣṣ) the elite, the chosen, the privileged portion
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses the broken plural כ'ואץ (khawāṣṣ) for the most-holy priestly portion — קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים-grade gifts assigned to Aaron's house in Numbers 18.

entries.gloss_en: wilderness, open uncultivated country, desert tract
entries.notes: From barr 'open country, dry land'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's alternate rendering of Hebrew מִדְבָּר alongside צחרא. Especially common in the construct 'wilderness of X' (ברייה' סיני, ברייה' פארן). Often interchangeable with صحراء (Saadia's צחרא).

entries.notes: Cognate with وَجْه 'face' but specialized to 'direction/side'. Distinct entry from וגה 'face/aspect'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses גהה for Hebrew פֵּאָה and רוּחַ 'side/quarter' in the boundary specifications of the tabernacle (Ex 26 ff.) and the land (Num 34, Ezek-style boundaries).

entries.gloss_en: totality, sum, whole; (in census) the head-count
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew רֹאשׁ in the census passages (שְׂאוּ אֶת רֹאשׁ → ארפעו גמלה). Renders the 'head' of the count, not a body-part.

entries.gloss_en: until, up to, even, so that
entries.notes: Subordinator + preposition. Followed by a verb in the subjunctive (purpose 'so that') or by a noun (terminus 'up to'). Distinct from حَتْم 'inevitable'.

entries.saadia_note: Saadia's standard gloss for Hebrew בְּאֵר — used in the patriarchal well-narratives and the Beer-Lahai-Roi / Beer-Sheba etymologies.

entries.gloss_en: leprous, afflicted with skin-disease; a leper
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew מְצֹרָע (one afflicted with צָרַעַת). The verbal root ברץ 'to be afflicted with skin-disease' shares ground with classical Arabic.
Saadia uses טרף for Hebrew קְצֵה in boundary descriptions; also for 'the edge of the territory' in the Edom-passage diplomacy of Num 20.

entries.gloss_en: Korah (son of Izhar, of the Kohathite Levites; led the rebellion in Numbers 16)
between, among; (with conjunction) on the one hand … on the other
entries.notes: Preposition of intermediate position. Often paired with a second بَيْن to express 'between X and Y'.

entries.gloss_en: right-hand, of the right side; (as noun) the right
entries.notes: Nisba adjective from يَمِين 'right'. Distinct from يَمَنِيّ 'Yemenite' though the surface form coincides.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses אלימני for Hebrew יָמִין 'right (side, thigh, shoulder)' — esp. priestly-portions in Lev 7 and Num 18.
Saadia uses מאל broadly for Hebrew רְכוּשׁ, חֵיל (substance), and מִקְנֶה (livestock as wealth).
Saadia's stock rendering of Hebrew תָּמִיד 'continually' — for the regular daily offerings (עֹלַת תָּמִיד) and the show-bread, and as a memorial-particle 'so that you remember always'.

entries.gloss_en: he passed through, traversed; (impersonal) it is permitted
entries.notes: Hollow verb jāza/yajūzu. The Form III جاوز means 'to overpass, transgress'. The impersonal لَا يَجُوز 'it is not permitted' is the legal idiom.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's primary gloss for Hebrew עָבַר in the through-the-territory diplomacy (Num 20–21) and the legal-permission idiom 'ולא יגוז אן…'.

entries.gloss_en: heart; (figuratively) mind, inner self; core, middle
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's standard gloss for Hebrew לֵב / לֵבָב. The 'hardening of the heart' idiom in the Exodus plague-cycle uses תשכך קלב X.

entries.gloss_en: or; (in interrogative) or rather; (after أ‑) the second alternative of a polar question
entries.notes: The disjunctive particle, distinct from أَو (=או) which is the open-list disjunction. Often introduces the second branch of an either-or question.
A Persian loanword (gūk) for 'troop, band'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses גוק for Hebrew קָהָל in the cultic-assembly passages — especially as a synonym of גמאעה in the מועד-trumpet calls (Num 10). Used by Saadia alongside גמאעה and עשירה for an organized group.

entries.gloss_en: curtain, hanging-veil (esp. of a tent or shrine)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew פָּרֹכֶת (the veil separating Holy from Holy-of-Holies). Distinct from חגאב which renders מָסָךְ (the outer screen).
Saadia's standard gloss for Hebrew רָעָב (famine) in the patriarchal-famine narratives and the Joseph-cycle.
Saadia uses אלמחאל / מחאלך for Hebrew שְׁעָרֶיךָ 'within your gates' (i.e. 'in your localities') in the Deuteronomy welfare and tithe passages.

entries.gloss_en: breastplate, chest-piece (the high priest's jeweled breast-ornament)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's standard gloss for Hebrew חֹשֶׁן הַמִּשְׁפָּט (the high-priestly judgment-breastplate set with twelve stones). Distinct from בדנה (= אֵפוֹד) which Saadia uses for the ephod.

entries.gloss_en: man, adult male; (broken pl. rijāl) men
entries.notes: Distinct from رِجْل 'foot/leg' (same root, different stem) — the foot-word is usually spelled the same in JA but disambiguates by context.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's primary gloss for Hebrew אִישׁ (adult male). Often paired with אמראה (woman). The broken pl. אלרגאל renders אֲנָשִׁים.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew קֶרֶב 'inwards' in the sacrificial-cuts passages (fat covering the entrails, the kidneys, the lobe of the liver).

entries.gloss_en: Reqem — the medieval Aramaic/Arabic identification of biblical קָדֵשׁ (Kadesh-barnea), the southern wilderness encampment
entries.notes: Matches the Targum Onqelos rendering of קָדֵשׁ. Petra in Greek-Roman tradition is also called Rekem in some sources.

entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew כְּבָשִׂים (lambs) in the festival-sacrifice prescriptions (Num 28–29).

entries.gloss_en: soul, self, person, life; (broken pl. nufūs) souls, persons
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's standard gloss for Hebrew נֶפֶשׁ in both the 'living being' and 'person' senses (e.g. קָתַל נֶפֶשׁ 'killed a person').

entries.gloss_en: knowing one, scholar, sage; (broken pl. ʿulamāʾ) scholars, the learned
entries.notes: Active participle of عَلِمَ 'to know'. Distinct from عَالَم 'world' though both forms can surface as עאלם.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses אלעלמא (the learned) for Hebrew שֹׁפְטִים and זִקְנֵי הָעֵדָה in judicial contexts.

entries.gloss_en: army, troop, military host; (broken pl. juyūsh) armies
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew צָבָא in its military sense (the host of fighting-men); for the cultic 'host of heaven' he prefers ג'נד / גמהור.

entries.gloss_en: servant, attendant; (in cultic context) one who ministers, performs service
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses כ'אדם for Hebrew מְשָׁרֵת (Joshua as Moses' attendant; the Levites' tabernacle service). The verb תכ'דם 'you serve' is standard for the priestly עֲבֹדָה.

entries.gloss_en: dye, coloring; (as verb) to dye, color, tint
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses צבג' in the leper-purification ritual (the cedar-wood, hyssop, and crimson dye of Lev 14 and Num 19) — for the Hebrew שָׁנִי (scarlet).
Saadia's standard gloss for Hebrew מַחֲצִית 'half' — the half-shekel census tax (Ex 30, 38) and divisions of sacrificial portions.

entries.gloss_en: one who knows; recognized authority; (broken pl. ʿurafāʾ) officers, recognized leaders
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ערפא (broken pl.) for Hebrew שֹׁטְרִים — the 'recognized ones' / sub-officers of the elders, especially in Num 11 and Deut 1.

entries.gloss_en: a time, an instance, an occurrence; (broken pl. marrāt / mirār) times
entries.notes: Distinct from the verb مَرَّ 'to pass' (separate entry) — though sharing the root, this noun-of-occurrence inflects on its own pattern.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew פַּעַם 'time, occurrence' — 'seven times' is rendered as סבע מראר.

entries.gloss_en: forever, perpetually, eternally; (in negative contexts) never, at all
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's stock rendering of Hebrew לְעוֹלָם 'forever' in the perpetual-decree formulae (חֻקַּת עוֹלָם → רסם אבדא).

entries.gloss_en: anger, wrath, indignation; (as verb) he became angry
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's standard gloss for the Hebrew divine-anger word-cluster (אַף, חֵמָה, חָרוֹן־אַף) — esp. the plague-passages in Numbers 11 and 25.

entries.gloss_en: other than, except; un‑ (negating prefix); a different one
entries.notes: Construct-state preposition: غَيْرُ X 'other than X'. Also negates a following noun ('ungod' = ג'יר אלאה).

entries.gloss_en: one who has entered (a community); resident-alien, sojourner; intruder, foreign element
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses אלדכ'יל alongside אלג'ריב for Hebrew גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב — the resident-alien class assimilated into Israel's communal law (Num 15:14–16, Lev 25:35).

entries.gloss_en: covering, lid, shroud (esp. a fitted cover laid over an object)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses אלג'שא for Hebrew כַּפֹּרֶת — the gold lid set above the ark of the testimony from which God speaks (Num 7:89). Distinct from his כַּפָּרָה 'expiation' (root k-f-r), which he renders by separate vocabulary.

entries.gloss_en: he made (it become), rendered, set, placed (causative of צאר)
entries.notes: Form II ṣayyara of the hollow verb ṣāra. The causative sense 'to make X into Y' takes a double accusative.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses צייר for Hebrew שׂוּם 'to set, place, render' — both physical (וַיַּשֶּׁם אֶת הָאָדָם, Gen 2:8 → וצייר ת'ם אדם) and figurative (made-into a sign, made-into a people).

entries.gloss_en: he washed (a body or object), rinsed clean
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's standard gloss for Hebrew רָחַץ in the purification-rituals — the priest's washing in the Levitical and Numerical purity-laws.

entries.gloss_en: with, in, by, by means of, against — proclitic preposition (Hebrew בְּ, Arabic bi-); appears almost exclusively with pronominal suffixes
entries.notes: Single-letter proclitic preposition. In the JA corpus the bare form is vanishingly rare; nearly all hits are pronominal-suffixed (בי 1s, בך 2ms, בה 3ms, בהא 3fs, בהם 3mp, בנא 1mp). Hebrew בְּ uses the same paradigm.

entries.saadia_note: Standard Arabic noun for moral evil; Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew רָע / רָעָה when used as an abstract or substantive ("the evil", "people of evil").

entries.gloss_en: flesh, meat, body (of an animal or human)
entries.notes: Standard Arabic for animal flesh / meat.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew בָּשָׂר (basar) when the sense is literal flesh / meat (vs. בָּשָׂר for "all flesh / humanity," where Saadia uses אנסאן or אלאנאם).

entries.gloss_en: guarding, keeping, charge, watch; the duty of safeguarding (a sacred object or place)
entries.notes: Verbal noun of ḥafiẓa "to guard, preserve." In manuscripts the trailing apostrophe (חפץ') marks the emphatic ẓ; the bare form חפץ appears when no apostrophe is written.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular calque for the priestly/Levitical Hebrew מִשְׁמֶרֶת — "the charge of the Tent of Meeting" (מִשְׁמֶרֶת אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד) becomes חפץ' מסכן אלשהאדה. The cognate verb יחפצון = יִשְׁמְרוּ.

entries.gloss_en: besides, except, apart from, other than; (also) equal, same
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew מִלְּבַד / לְבַד מִן in census and offering contexts (e.g. Bamidbar 17 "besides those who died on account of Korah"; Bamidbar 29 "besides the daily offering"). Arabic siwā "other than, except." When tallying populations or sacrifices, Saadia uses סוא X to mean "not counting X / besides X.".

entries.gloss_en: Bashan — the medieval Arabic name (al-Baṭaniyya) for biblical בָּשָׁן, the land east of the Jordan ruled by Og
entries.notes: Geographic identification: al-Baṭaniyya is the early-medieval Arabic toponym for the basaltic plateau of Bashan in the Hauran. The trailing י־ה renders the Arabic feminine ending -iyya.

entries.gloss_en: measure, amount, quantity, extent, proportion; (in idiom ʿalā qadr-) according to, in proportion to
entries.notes: Arabic qadr "amount, extent." The idiom עלי' קדר X = "in proportion to X / according to X" — used for apportioning inheritance, conscription, and offerings (Bamidbar 26, 35).
Standard Arabic noun.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's invariable gloss for Hebrew קוֹל (qol) — whether the cry of a child (Bereshit 21:17), the voice of Jacob (Bereshit 27:22), the sound of God walking in the garden (Bereshit 3:8), or the people's outcry to God (Bamidbar 20:16). The trailing-tav consonant ת renders Arabic emphatic t (ṭ in some manuscripts is written ט; Saadia generally writes ת).

entries.gloss_en: tomorrow, the morrow, the next day
entries.notes: Arabic ghad with apostrophe ג' marking the ghayn. The phrase אלי' ג'ד = "to / by tomorrow." The form ג'דהם (their morrow / the next day for them) is a possessive idiom.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מָחָר (maḥar). Bamidbar 11:18 "prepare yourselves for tomorrow" (הִתְקַדְּשׁוּ לְמָחָר) = אסתעדו אלי' ג'ד.

entries.gloss_en: tenth (of an ephah); a dry-measure unit (~2 L); (pl.) tithes
entries.notes: Arabic ʿushr "a tenth." In sacrificial contexts (Bamidbar 15, 28-29) ת'לאת'ה' עשור = "three-tenths" of fine flour for a grain offering. In Bamidbar 18 עשור = "the tithe."
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew עִשָּׂרוֹן (issaron, the tenth-ephah grain measure) and for מַעֲשֵׂר (tithe) — both rendered with the same Arabic root.

entries.gloss_en: second through tenth ordinals (ت'اني 2nd, ثالث 3rd, رابع 4th, خامس 5th, سادس 6th, سابع 7th, ثامن 8th, تاسع 9th, عاشر 10th); used for days of the month, sacrificial days, calendar dates
entries.gloss_he: סִדּוּרִיִּים: שֵׁנִי, שְׁלִישִׁי, רְבִיעִי, חֲמִישִׁי, שִׁשִּׁי, שְׁבִיעִי, שְׁמִינִי, תְּשִׁיעִי, עֲשִׂירִי
entries.notes: The ordinal "first" (אוול) already lives in starter.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses the Arabic ordinal paradigm for Hebrew calendar/day-N references — e.g. Bamidbar 28-29 sacrificial calendar, Bamidbar 7 leaders by day.

entries.gloss_en: enemy, foe, adversary; (broken pl. ʔaʿdāʔ) enemies
entries.notes: Singular ʿaduww; broken plural ʔaʿdāʔ takes pronominal suffixes (אעדאי "my enemies," אעדאיכם "your enemies," אעדאהם "their enemies").
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew אוֹיֵב / אֹיֵב — Bamidbar 10:9 "when you go to war against your enemies" = אד'א צרתם אלי' חרב מע אלעדו ... תג'אתון מן אעדאיכם.

entries.gloss_en: generation, age, era; (broken pl. ʔajyāl) generations
entries.notes: Singular jīl; broken plural ʔajyāl. The expression מר אגיאלכם / לאגיאלכם = "throughout your generations."
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew דּוֹר (dor) — Bamidbar 10:8 "a perpetual statute throughout your generations" (חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם) = רסם אלדהר לאגיאלכם.

entries.gloss_en: commandment, injunction, charge, instruction; (broken pl. waṣāyā) commandments
entries.notes: Singular waṣiyya; broken plural waṣāyā renders as וצאיא. The form וצאיאה = "his commandments" (3ms suffix on broken pl.).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מִצְוָה / מִצְוֹת — Devarim 10:13, 11:1 "keep his commandments" (וּלִשְׁמֹר אֶת־מִצְוֹתָיו) = ואחפץ' וצאיאה.

Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew רֵעַ when the context is social/legal — Devarim 13:7 "or your companion who is as your own soul" = או צאחבך אלד'י הו כנפסך; Devarim 19:14 "you shall not move your neighbor's boundary" = לא תזייג' תכ'ם צאחבך. Standard Arabic ṣāḥib "companion." Saadia uses it where the Hebrew has the social-relation sense of רֵעַ ("the fellow Israelite," "your neighbor").
Saadia uses the Hebrew root גרש directly as a Judeo-Arabic verb. The standard classical Arabic equivalents are ṭarada (طرد) and akhraja (أخرج).

entries.gloss_en: burning, incineration (especially of a sacrificial animal)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia adopts the Hebrew noun שְׂרֵפָה (śərēfā) directly. The classical Arabic equivalents are ḥarq (حرق) and iḥrāq (إحراق).

In classical Arabic ḥajj specifically denotes the pilgrimage. Saadia uses חג as the regular gloss for Hebrew חַג (any of the three pilgrimage festivals Pesach, Shavuot, Sukkot — and by extension any festival).

entries.gloss_en: unleavened bread; freshly-baked dough that has not risen — matzah
that which is brought near; (technical) an offering, sacrifice
entries.notes: Form-II passive participle of qarraba 'to bring near'. Active muqarrib = 'one who brings near'; passive muqarrab = 'that which is brought near'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses muqarrab as the regular technical gloss for Hebrew קָרְבָּן (offering, sacrifice).

entries.gloss_en: wild beast, predator, untamed animal (game animals of the open country)
entries.notes: Leading ו is the root letter (w-ḥ-sh), NOT the conjunction prefix. Surface form is identical to a hypothetical w-prefixed ḥash.

entries.gloss_en: smaller, younger; (with article) the smallest, the youngest
entries.gloss_he: קטן יותר, צעיר יותר; הקטן, הצעיר
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew הַקָּטֹן in narrative passages (e.g. Esau-Jacob; Joseph and his brothers).

entries.gloss_en: except, besides, apart from, with the exception of
entries.notes: Distinct from sawa سِوَى (root s-w-y, also 'besides') — both can render Hebrew זוּלָתִי / מִלְּבַד.

entries.gloss_en: so that not, lest, in order that not
entries.notes: Compound particle: purposive kay + negative lā.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew פֶּן.

entries.gloss_en: remembrance, memorial, reminder; a thing called to mind
resident, dweller, one who resides or stays in a place
qist — a measure of capacity (about half a hin / quarter of a kor); also: justice, equity, fairness
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses qisṭ as the regular gloss for Hebrew הִין (the Tabernacle liquid-measure).

entries.gloss_en: estate, landed property, plot of land, field, village or rural settlement
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ḍayʿa as the regular gloss for Hebrew שָׂדֶה in property/legal and topographic contexts (e.g. Gen 23 Machpelah, Num 23 Balaam's heights).

entries.gloss_en: gift, present, offering brought to a superior or to God
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses hadiyya as one regular gloss for Hebrew מִנְחָה (gift, offering), especially in non-cultic contexts (Cain in Gen 4, Jacob's gift to Esau in Gen 32).

entries.gloss_en: the Torah — the Five Books of Moses, the Mosaic Law
the open country, the wilderness, the wide expanse outside settled areas
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses al-ṣaḥrā' for Hebrew הַשָּׂדֶה in the sense of 'open country / wilderness' (e.g. Exod 22:30 'flesh torn in the field').

entries.gloss_en: a length of fabric, a panel, a curtain (especially of woven cloth or felt)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses shuqqa as the regular gloss for Hebrew יְרִיעָה (the Tabernacle curtains, Exod 26).
In sacrificial contexts קרבאן אלאת'ם renders Hebrew אָשָׁם (guilt-offering).

entries.gloss_en: an act of ritual slaughter; a sin-offering, the purification offering
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ḏakwa as the regular gloss for Hebrew חַטָּאת (sin-offering). In classical Arabic the underlying root denotes ritual slaughter (ḏakāh). Saadia, technical — the sin-offering.

entries.gloss_en: the far side, the trans-(river) region; (in construct, e.g. עבר הירדן) across the Jordan
entries.notes: Homograph with the classical Arabic verb ʿabara 'he crossed' (root ʿ-b-r) — context disambiguates.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew noun עֵבֶר ('side, beyond') in the construct phrase עבר אלארדן for the trans-Jordanian region.

entries.gloss_en: amen — so be it; (affirmation of oaths and curses)

entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ṣaḥīḥ as the regular gloss for Hebrew תָּמִים in sacrificial contexts ('without blemish').

entries.gloss_en: to answer, to reply, to respond
to look, to see, to observe, to behold
entries.notes: Surface אנצ'ר covers both 1ms imperfect 'anẓuru ('I look') and the imperative unẓur ('look!') — context disambiguates.

entries.gloss_en: to see, to look at, to perceive, to behold
to call, to summon, to invoke, to pray; (as noun duʿā') a call, prayer, supplication
entries.gloss_he: קרא, קרא בשם, התפלל; (כשם עצם) תפילה, קריאה
entries.notes: Homograph: the surface דעא covers both the perfect verb daʿā ('he called') and the verbal noun duʿā' ('prayer'). Context disambiguates.

entries.gloss_en: (with preceding mā) except, save for, apart from
entries.notes: Construction מא כ'לא (mā khalā) functions as 'except, save for'. The verb khalā literally means 'to be empty / devoid (of)'.

entries.gloss_en: to give a name to, to name, to call (someone) by a name
to lay (a hand) upon; to lean upon, support, prop
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses sanada as the regular gloss for Hebrew סָמַךְ in the 'laying of hands' on a sacrifice (Exod 29:10, Lev 1:4 and parallels).

entries.gloss_en: at that time, then, in that moment
entries.notes: Compound demonstrative adverb: ḥīna (time) + iḏ (when/that-time).

entries.gloss_en: to go, to proceed, to pass on, to go forth, to elapse
to remain, to be left over, to endure; (as proper noun) Bukki (a personal name, Num 34:22)
entries.notes: Homograph: the verb baqiya and the biblical proper noun Bukki share the same surface form. Context disambiguates.

entries.gloss_en: to attain, to reach, to obtain, to acquire, to come into possession of
entries.gloss_he: השיג, השיגה ידו, הגיע ל-, רכש
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses 'mā tanāl yad-' as the regular gloss for Hebrew הִשִּׂיגָה יָדוֹ / כְּפִי מַתְּנַת יָדוֹ ('within his means', 'according to what his hand can attain').

entries.gloss_en: to swear (an oath), to take an oath, to make a solemn pledge
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses aqsama as the regular gloss for Hebrew נִשְׁבַּע, especially in 'God's oath to the patriarchs' formulations.
Used by Saadia alongside qawm and umma for Hebrew עַם — especially in poetic and oracular contexts (e.g. Balaam's oracles, Num 23).

entries.gloss_en: Sabbath, the day of rest, Saturday
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew form סבת for שַׁבָּת. The Arabic cognate sabt has the same denotation but is more limited in classical usage to 'Saturday'.

entries.gloss_en: box, chest, casket, ark; a wooden or metal container with a lid
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ṣundūq as the regular gloss for Hebrew אָרוֹן (the Ark of the Covenant; the box for the broken tablets, Deut 10:2).

entries.gloss_en: bowl, dish, large basin (especially for serving food or holding offerings)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses qaṣʿa as the regular gloss for Hebrew קְעָרָה (the silver basin of each tribal offering, Num 7:13ff).

entries.gloss_en: yesterday; (in the construction mithl ams) as before, as in time past
good, goodness, benefit, prosperity; (in comparative usage) better
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses khayr as the regular gloss for Hebrew טוֹב in moral and beneficent senses ('do good', 'God planned good').

entries.gloss_en: life, lifetime, age, span of life
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ʿumr as the regular gloss for Hebrew יָמִים / שְׁנֵי חַיִּים in genealogical age formulas ('all the days of his life').

entries.gloss_en: tablet, plank, board, slab (especially of stone or wood)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses lawḥ as the regular gloss for Hebrew לוּחַ (the tablets of stone at Sinai; Deut 10:1-3).
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew אָרוּר, especially in the Mount Ebal curses (Deut 27).

entries.gloss_en: rest, day of rest, cessation from work, holiday
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ʿuṭla as the regular gloss for Hebrew שַׁבָּתוֹן, pairing with sabt to render the full phrase שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן (e.g. Exod 16:23; 31:15).
Saadia uses al-maʿdūdīn as the regular gloss for Hebrew הַפְּקֻדִים (those numbered in the wilderness census, Num 1-4).
Saadia uses al-a'imma (pl. of imām) as the regular gloss for Hebrew הַכֹּהֲנִים (the priests / sons of Aaron). The singular imām renders הַכֹּהֵן. Saadia — the priests.

entries.gloss_en: eyes; springs of water; (in textual usage) the letters or contents of a written text
entries.gloss_he: עיניים; מעיינות מים; (לטקסט כתוב) אותיות הכתוב
entries.notes: Broken plural of ʿayn ('eye, spring, source').
entries.saadia_note: In the Mount Ebal stone-engraving passage (Deut 27:3, 8), Saadia uses עיון הד'ה אלתורייה for 'the words/letters of this Torah'. Saadia uses ʿuyūn in three distinct senses: (1) eyes — perception/awareness; (2) springs — water sources; (3) text — the letters/words of a written document.

entries.gloss_en: border, boundary, frontier, limit of a territory
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses takhm as the regular gloss for Hebrew גְּבוּל (territorial border).
Saadia uses wādī as the regular gloss for Hebrew נַחַל (valley / seasonal watercourse).

entries.gloss_en: filled, full (especially: filled with a specified substance)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses mamlū' as the regular gloss for Hebrew מָלֵא in the tribal-gift incense-spoon formula (Num 7:14ff: 'a gold spoon filled with incense').

entries.gloss_en: war, battle, armed conflict, military campaign
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ḥarb as the regular gloss for Hebrew מִלְחָמָה.

In the festival prohibition 'kull ṣanʿat maksab lā taʿmalū', Saadia renders Hebrew כָּל מְלֶאכֶת עֲבֹדָה לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ ('no work-of-acquisition shall you perform') — distinguishing servile work from food-preparation labor allowed on Yom Tov.

entries.gloss_en: Passover — the festival commemorating the Exodus from Egypt
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew form פסח for the festival. The Arabic cognate fish (الفِصْح) is used for the Christian Easter; Saadia avoids it.

entries.gloss_en: gum, resin (especially aromatic resin used as incense)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses al-ṣamgh as the regular gloss for Hebrew לְבֹנָה (frankincense — the aromatic resin in the Tabernacle incense, Exod 30:34; Num 4:16).

entries.gloss_en: an anointing, an act of smearing with oil; (in construct) oil-of-anointing
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses dahn al-masḥ as the regular gloss for Hebrew שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה (the anointing oil, Exod 25:6 and parallels).

entries.gloss_en: hair (collective: the hair of a head, body, or animal)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses shaʿr as the regular gloss for Hebrew שֵׂעָר (especially in Nazirite passages, Num 6).

entries.gloss_en: a small container or ladle; an incense-spoon
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses darj as the regular gloss for Hebrew כַּף (the gold incense-spoon of each tribal offering, Num 7:14ff).
Saadia uses baqara as the regular gloss for Hebrew פָּרָה. The collective al-baqar renders הַבָּקָר ('the cattle').

entries.gloss_en: a taking possession, a holding, a possessed inheritance
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses li-taḥawwuz as the regular gloss for Hebrew לִירֻשָּׁה / לְמוֹרָשָׁה ('as a possession' — the patriarchal promise of the land, Gen 15:7; Deut 11:10).

entries.notes: Homograph with ibnahu 'his son' (m. + suffix). Context disambiguates. The explicit feminine form ibnatuhu (אבנתה) is unambiguous.

entries.gloss_en: Horeb — the mountain of Sinai (the alternative name in Deuteronomy)
a plank, a wooden board (a Tabernacle plank)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses takhtaja as the regular gloss for Hebrew קֶרֶשׁ (the upright planks of the Tabernacle, Exod 26:15ff). The form is a Persian loanword (takhtah 'plank') Arabicized with a feminine ending.

entries.gloss_en: around, surrounding, on all sides of
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ḥawālay as the regular gloss for Hebrew סָבִיב (around).

entries.gloss_en: if (contrary-to-fact); if only; were it that
entries.notes: Distinct from in (إِنْ), which marks open conditional ('if X happens'). law marks counterfactual or hypothetical ('if only X had happened').

entries.gloss_en: Jebusite — descendant of Jebus (= Jerusalem); the pre-Israelite inhabitants of the city
a vow, a votive pledge, a thing dedicated by oath
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses naḏr as the regular gloss for Hebrew נֶדֶר. The verb tasawwagha naḏran ('to fulfill a vow') glosses לְפַלֵּא נֶדֶר.

entries.gloss_en: to rise, to stand up, to arise; (imperative) arise! get up!
to be next to, to face, to follow; (in construction 'mā yalī') what is next to / what faces
entries.gloss_he: עמד מול, פנה אל, היה סמוך ל-; (במבנה 'מא ילי') מול, לעומת
entries.saadia_note: Surface ילי (yalī, 3ms impf) appears most often in the construction 'mā yalī' = 'what faces, what is opposite' — Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אֶל מוּל ('toward, opposite').

entries.gloss_en: a sheep, a head of small livestock (sheep or goat)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses shāh as the regular gloss for Hebrew שֶׂה (a single head of small livestock).
Saadia uses ʿaṣā as the regular gloss for Hebrew מַטֶּה (the tribal rods, Num 17; Moses' staff).

entries.gloss_en: plains, level wildernesses (plural of bayḍāʾ 'desert plain')
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses bīdāt as the regular gloss for Hebrew עַרְבוֹת (the plains of Moab, the Aravah, Num 22:1; 33:48ff).

entries.gloss_en: fullness, the full content of (a container)
entries.saadia_note: In the construction 'milʾ bayti-hi (faḍḍatan wa-dhahaban)' = '(equivalent to) his house full (of silver and gold)' — Saadia's gloss for Hebrew מְלֹא בֵיתוֹ (Num 22:18; 24:13).

entries.gloss_en: possession, the act of taking possession or holding
entries.notes: Bare Form-I verbal noun. The Form-V verbal noun taḥawwuz (see taHawwuz-possession) carries the same sense.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ḥawz as the regular gloss for Hebrew יְרֻשָּׁה / מוֹרָשָׁה ('inheritance, possession of land', Num 27:7; 32:32).

entries.gloss_en: witness, one who testifies; one who is present
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses shāhid as the regular gloss for Hebrew עֵד (witness) in legal contexts (Num 35:30; Deut 19:15).

entries.gloss_en: craft, work, labor, manufacture; an act of making
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ṣināʿa as the regular gloss for Hebrew מְלָאכָה (work, especially the Tabernacle's prohibited Sabbath labor and the priestly service-labor of Num 4:3).
Saadia uses al-ṣanāʾiʿ as the regular gloss for Hebrew הַמְּלָאכוֹת in plural festival/Sabbath-prohibition contexts ('any of the labors' — Exod 12:16; Deut 5:14).

entries.gloss_en: dārush — the dyed-skin covering of the Tabernacle (Hebrew תַּחַשׁ)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses dārush as the regular gloss for Hebrew תַּחַשׁ (the mysterious outer-covering skins of the Tabernacle, Exod 25:5; Num 4:6). The classical Arabic identification is uncertain; medieval commentators connect it to Persian darshī ('a kind of dyed leather') or Aramaic תַּחְשָׁא.

entries.gloss_en: shaking, moving, waving (Form-II verbal noun of ḥarraka)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses taḥrīk as the regular gloss for Hebrew תְּנוּפָה (the wave-offering, Exod 29:24; Num 6:20).

entries.gloss_en: Shem — the eldest son of Noah; ancestor of the Semitic peoples
entries.notes: Homograph with Hebrew שֵׁם ('name') and שָׁם ('there').
entries.saadia_note: Context disambiguates — in Saadia's tafsir the surface שם most often refers to the patriarch.

entries.gloss_en: price, value, payment in money; (with bi-) for a price, bought with money
entries.saadia_note: In 'al-mushtarī bi-thaman' (Gen 17:12-13), Saadia renders Hebrew מִקְנַת כֶּסֶף ('purchased with silver').

entries.gloss_en: to stretch out, to extend, to reach out (especially of the hand)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses madda as the regular gloss for Hebrew שָׁלַח (to send out / stretch out one's hand, Gen 19:10; 22:10).

entries.gloss_en: leader, commander, chief, one who leads
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses al-quwwād (broken plural of qā'id) as one regular gloss for Hebrew הָעֲבָדִים / שָׂרִים when these denote officials and military officers (Gen 20:8; 40:20).

entries.gloss_en: the lower part, the bottom; below, beneath
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses asfal as the regular gloss for Hebrew תַּחַת in expressions of 'beneath, under' (Gen 35:8 'beneath Bethel'; Deut 32:22 'the depths of the earth').

entries.gloss_en: eye; spring of water; (in textual usage) the letter or visible mark of a written text
entries.notes: The broken plural ʿuyūn covers the same range — see ʿuyun-eyes-springs.

entries.gloss_en: curtain, hanging cloth (especially a courtyard or sail-cloth)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses qulūʿ (pl. of qilāʿ) as the regular gloss for Hebrew קְלָעִים (the courtyard hangings of the Tabernacle, Exod 27:9ff).
Lexicalized imperative — historically the imperative of taʿālā 'to be exalted', but used in classical Arabic and Saadia's JA as a bare 'come!' Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew לְכָה / לֵךְ.

entries.gloss_en: to be long, to last long, to endure
entries.gloss_he: ארך, נמשך זמן רב, האריך ימים
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ṭāla as the regular gloss for Hebrew אָרַךְ in 'that your days may be long' (Deut 11:9; 11:21).

entries.gloss_en: to strike, to beat, to hit; (idiomatic) to utter (a parable or proverb)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ḍaraba mathalan as the regular gloss for Hebrew נָשָׂא מָשָׁל ('to take up a parable', Balaam's oracles, Num 23-24).

entries.gloss_en: to return, to come back, to go back; (intransitive) to revert, to turn back
to prostrate oneself, to bow down (especially in worship or homage)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses sajada as the regular gloss for Hebrew הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה / כָּרַע (to bow / prostrate, especially in worship or before a superior).

entries.gloss_en: distance, the extent of a journey, a stretch of road
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses masāfa in 'masāfat aḥada ʿashara yawman' as the gloss for Hebrew אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם — the eleven-day march from Horeb to Kadesh-Barnea (Deut 1:2).

entries.notes: Homograph: bayḍāʾ 'white (f.)' and bayḍa 'an egg' share the surface ביצ'א. Context disambiguates.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses bayḍāʾ as the regular gloss for Hebrew לְבָנָה ('white as snow', e.g. Miriam's tsaraat at Num 12:10) and bayḍa for Hebrew בֵּיצָה (egg, Deut 22:6).

entries.gloss_en: mighty one, giant, tyrant; (broken plural jabābira) the giants
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses al-jabābira as the regular gloss for Hebrew הָעֲנָקִים / הַנְּפִילִים (the giants/Anakim of Num 13).

entries.gloss_en: stones (collective: stones, rocks, especially for building or stoning)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses al-ḥijāra as the regular gloss for Hebrew אֲבָנִים in stoning-as-punishment contexts (Num 14:10; 15:35).

entries.gloss_en: left; to the left; the left side
entries.notes: Paired with יִמְנָה (yimna 'right') in 'lā yamīl yamna wa-lā yasra' = 'he does not turn right or left'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses yasra as the regular gloss for Hebrew שְׂמֹאל ('left') in the orientation formula לֹא תָסוּר יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאל.

entries.gloss_en: Hor — the mountain where Aaron died (Num 20:22; 33:38); a peak in Edom
Nadab — son of Aaron, killed for offering strange fire (Lev 10; Num 3:4; 26:60-61)

entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses bayna al-ghurūbayn ('between the two sunsets') as the regular gloss for Hebrew בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם — the late-afternoon window of the daily evening sacrifice (Exod 12:6; Num 28:4ff).

entries.gloss_he: מזיגה, משקה מהול; (במונח קרבני) נסך, מנחת נסך
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses mizāj as the regular gloss for Hebrew נֶסֶךְ (the wine drink-offering accompanying sacrifices, Num 15:7-10; 28:7-10). Saadia, technical — a libation, a drink-offering.

entries.gloss_en: meadow, pasture, open plain (especially associated with a notable tree or oak)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses marj as the regular gloss for Hebrew אֵלוֹן / אֵלֵי X ('the oak of...', e.g. marj Mamrē for אֵלוֹנֵי מַמְרֵא; marj Shittim for Abel-Shittim, Num 33:49).

entries.gloss_en: great, large; (with article in technical contexts) the Great One — Mediterranean, elder, etc.
entries.saadia_note: In 'al-baḥr al-kabīr' Saadia renders Hebrew הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל ('the Great Sea' = the Mediterranean, Num 34:6-7).

entries.gloss_en: khurnūb — a small silver sprinkling-bowl or basin
entries.gloss_he: מזרק (קערית כסף קטנה, אחת מכלי המקדש)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses khurnūb as the regular gloss for Hebrew מִזְרָק (the silver sprinkling-bowl of each tribal offering, Num 7:13ff). Paired with qaṣʿa (the larger basin).

entries.gloss_en: mixed, kneaded, mingled (passive participle of latta 'to mix into dough')
entries.notes: Homograph with a variant on millet-religion (likely an earlier mis-tag). Distinct lexical entry: lattē 'mixing dry with wet'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses maltūt(an) bi-duhn as the regular gloss for Hebrew בְּלוּלָה בַשֶּׁמֶן ('mingled with oil' — the grain-offering, Num 6:15; Exod 29:2).

entries.gloss_en: to uncover, to reveal, to disclose; to expose what was concealed
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses kashafa as the regular gloss for Hebrew גִּלָּה in 'uncovering nakedness' (ʿerwa) prohibitions (Lev 18; Exod 20:23).

entries.gloss_en: to promise, to make a pledge, to give one's word
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses waʿada as the regular gloss for Hebrew דִּבֶּר / נִשְׁבַּע in the patriarchal-promise formula ('as the LORD has promised', Deut 1:21; 12:20).
In the farewell 'bi-salām' Saadia renders Hebrew בְּשָׁלוֹם (Gen 15:15; Gen 26:29 'we sent you away in peace').

entries.gloss_en: living, alive; (with article) the Living One — an attribute of God
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses al-ḥayy as the regular gloss for Hebrew חַי in 'God the Living' (e.g. Deut 5:23 'the voice of the living God'; Gen 16:14 'the Well of the Living One who sees').
Saadia uses lawḥay jawhar as the regular gloss for Hebrew לוּחֹת הָאֲבָנִים (the stone tablets of the Decalogue, Deut 5:19; 9:9). Saadia — the dressed stone of the Decalogue tablets.

entries.gloss_en: table, banquet-table (especially one set with food)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses al-mā'ida as the regular gloss for Hebrew הַשֻּׁלְחָן — the Tabernacle Table of Showbread (Exod 25:23ff).
In 'zā'idat al-kabid' Saadia renders Hebrew יוֹתֶרֶת הַכָּבֵד ('the appendage / lobe of the liver', Exod 29:13, 22; Lev 3:4).

entries.gloss_en: kidney (the organ; dual: the two kidneys)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses al-kulwatayn (dual) as the regular gloss for Hebrew הַכְּלָיֹת (the two kidneys of the sacrificial animal, Exod 29:13; Lev 3:4).
Saadia uses al-ḍafādiʿ (broken pl.) as the regular gloss for Hebrew הַצְּפַרְדְּעִים (the Exodus plague of frogs, Exod 7-8).

entries.gloss_en: one who is purifying himself, one undergoing purification rites
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses al-mutaṭahhir as the regular gloss for Hebrew הַמִּטַּהֵר (the leper undergoing post-quarantine purification, Lev 14:7-8).

entries.gloss_en: shameful part, private parts, nakedness; (idiomatic) shame, disgrace
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses sawʾa as the regular gloss for Hebrew עֶרְוָה (nakedness, especially in the Lev 18 prohibitions and Exod 20:23 altar-steps).
Saadia uses ʿadad as the regular gloss for Hebrew הַפְּקֻדִים / מִסְפַּר in census formulas (Num 1; Num 26).

entries.gloss_en: the south, the southern direction; (in compass formulas) southward
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses al-janūb as the regular gloss for Hebrew נֶגֶב / דָּרוֹם (the southward direction, Num 2:10; 10:6).

entries.gloss_en: Merari — third son of Levi; ancestor of the Merarite Levitical clan

entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ḥamū as the regular gloss for Hebrew חוֹתֵן (especially Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, Exod 18:7; Num 10:29).
Saadia uses ghulām as the regular gloss for Hebrew נַעַר (especially the 'servant-lad' Hobab/Joshua and Abraham's servant-lad of Gen 18:7).

entries.gloss_en: Adah — (1) Lamech's first wife (Gen 4:19ff); (2) Esau's Hittite wife (Gen 36:2)
entries.notes: Homograph with the noun ʿidda 'count, number' (see ʿadad-number entry). Context disambiguates.
Plural ratt-ūt (Blau §1367 notes the form ratt + plural rutūt likely reflects a mistaken pointing tradition; the underlying Arabic etymology is unsettled).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew פַר (par, 'young bull') in sacrificial passages — distinct from ת'ור (thawr), which translates שׁוֹר ('ox'). Plural רת'ות' / רתות' renders פָּרִים.

entries.gloss_en: to finish, complete, conclude (an activity); to be done with
entries.notes: Often construed with min ('from') + verbal noun: faragha min al-kalām = 'he finished speaking'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for the participial-temporal Hebrew construction 'when X had finished doing Y' (כְּכַלֹּתוֹ / וַיְכַל) — e.g. ולמא פרג' מוסי' מן נצב אלמסכן (Num 7:1) = 'when Moses had finished setting up the tabernacle.'

entries.gloss_en: to forgive, pardon, cover over (a fault, sin)
entries.notes: Distinct from the Form-X istaghfara (יסתג'פר 'to seek forgiveness') which is already in the dictionary.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew סָלַח (e.g. Num 15:28 ויג'פר לה = וְסָלַח לוֹ; Deut 32:43 ויג'פר לבלאדה).

entries.gloss_en: to step forward, advance, come forward, present oneself; to take precedence
entries.notes: Form V (تَفَعَّل) of q-d-m. Often used narratively: 'so-and-so came forward (and said/did X).'
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses tafriʿ-form taqaddama for Hebrew narrative 'rose up / stood up / came forward' constructions, especially in the Korah pericope (Num 16:1 פתקדם קרח) and in Moses-and-Aaron advancing toward the tent (Num 17:8).

entries.gloss_en: to leave (alone); to let go; to release, dismiss
entries.notes: Form II (خَلَّى) of kh-l-w. With 3ms object suffix: khallāhu = 'he left him' / 'he let him alone'.

entries.gloss_en: to cover, veil, conceal; (as noun) covering, screen, curtain
entries.notes: Both verbal and nominal uses attested.
entries.saadia_note: Nominal sitr / satr = 'screen, curtain' — Saadia uses it for the מָסָךְ of the Tabernacle entrance (Num 3:25-26: וסתר באב כ'בא אלמחצ'ר 'and the screen of the door of the Tent of Meeting').
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew דְּבַשׁ — appears in the recurring formula 'a land flowing with milk and honey' (אַרֶץ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ → בלד יפיץ' אללבן ואלעסל).

entries.gloss_en: sheep, flock of sheep (as opposed to goats — ma'z)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew כֶּבֶשׂ / כְּבָשִׂים in many sacrificial passages, distinct from kabsh (כבש, individual ram) and ghanam (ג'נם, generic 'flock'). Often paired with ma'z (goats) in offering passages — Saadia uses the two together to render Hebrew כבשים-ועזים collocations.

entries.gloss_en: inadvertence, oversight, unintentional act; (adv. accusative sahwan) inadvertently, by mistake
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew שְׁגָגָה (inadvertent sin) in Lev 4 and Num 15:22-28 — especially the adverbial accusative סהוא = 'inadvertently' rendering Heb בִּשְׁגָגָה. The active participle אלסאהי ('the inadvertent one') glosses Heb הַשֹּׁגֵג.

Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מַגֵּפָה (plague) — most prominently the plague that broke out after Baal Peor (Num 17:13-14: ואנחבס אלובא 'and the plague was stopped') and the plague at the spies' return (Num 14).
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אֶצְבַּע. Most frequently appears in the ritual formula 'and he shall dip his finger in the blood' — באצבעה ('with his finger', Num 19:4; Lev 14:16).
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מֵת as a noun (the dead person, the corpse). Distinct from the verbal sense, which Saadia renders with the verb māta (מאת).
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew חֶרֶב. The phrase בחד אלסיף ('with the edge of the sword') renders Heb לְפִי-חֶרֶב in conquest narratives (e.g. Num 21:24; Gen 34:26).

Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew רִיב in disputes between persons or households (e.g. Gen 13:7-8: וכאנת כ'צומה בין רעא מאשיה' אברם 'and there was a quarrel between the herdsmen of Abram's livestock').

entries.notes: Distinct from the verb khallā 'to leave alone'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew זֹאת / דָּבָר in legal-exhortative formulas: 'do this matter' = אצנעו כ'לה (Num 16:6, Gen 42:18). Blau §1085 documents the pattern across many Saadianic biblical translations. Post-classical / Judeo-Arabic usage; extensively attested in Saadia (Blau §1085).

entries.notes: Arabic gender polarity: khamsa (with tā' marbūṭa) counts masculine nouns; khams counts feminine. Note JA spelling כמסה lacks the apostrophe-marked خ — scribal convention varies.
Arabic gender polarity: thamāniya (with tā' marbūṭa) counts masculine nouns; thamānin counts feminine.

entries.gloss_en: how much? how many? how long?
entries.notes: Interrogative for quantity or duration. In the construction 'ilā kam' = 'until when / how long', it renders Heb עַד-אָנָה (Num 14:11, 14:27 אלי' כם אבקי 'how long shall I endure').
Distal plural demonstrative. The proximal counterpart is hāʾulāʾ (האולאי) 'these'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses both regularly.

entries.gloss_en: facing, opposite, parallel to, alongside; over against
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses ḥidhāʾa as a spatial preposition for 'facing / alongside / opposite' — e.g. Num 2:2 חד'א כ'בא אלמחצ'ר 'facing the Tent of Meeting' (Heb נֶגֶד); Num 25:4 חד'א אלשמס 'in the open, facing the sun' (Heb נֶגֶד הַשָּׁמֶשׁ).

entries.gloss_en: Caleb (son of Jephunneh, spy from the tribe of Judah)
entries.notes: Homograph with classical Arabic kalb 'dog' (which has root k-l-b).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged. In the Pentateuch's JA tafsir, every attested כלב refers to Caleb — context disambiguates.

entries.gloss_en: Er — (1) son of Judah (Gen 38); (2) Ar (or 'Er Moab'), a Moabite city east of the Arnon (Num 21:15, 21:28; Deut 2:9, 2:18, 2:29)
entries.gloss_he: עֵר — (1) בנו של יהודה; (2) עָר־מוֹאָב, עיר מואבית
entries.notes: In the Pentateuch the homograph context is almost always the Moabite city Ar, not Judah's firstborn — the latter appears once in Num 26:19.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew form unchanged for both senses.

entries.gloss_en: Abihu — second son of Aaron, killed for offering 'strange fire' (Lev 10; Num 3:4, 26:60-61)
entries.notes: Always paired with נדב (Nadab) in the Pentateuchal narrative formulas.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged.

entries.gloss_en: husband, master, lord; possessor (of a thing)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew בַּעַל / אִישׁ in marriage contexts (e.g. the vows pericope, Num 30:7-15: בעלהא 'her husband').

entries.gloss_en: to cause to alight, settle, or dwell; to make (a thing) descend or repose (in a place)
entries.notes: Form IV (أَحَلَّ) of ḥ-l-l. The Form-I yaḥull means 'to alight, descend' intransitively; Form IV is transitive.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for the recurring Deuteronomic formula 'the place where YHWH will cause his name to dwell' (לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם) — rendered אן יחל נורה פיה / ליחל נורה פיה 'that he may cause his light to alight there' (Deut 12:5, 12:11, 14:23, 14:24, etc., with the characteristic anti-anthropomorphic substitution of nūr 'light' for šēm 'name').

entries.gloss_en: to be / become ritually pure, clean (of persons, vessels, garments)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew טָהֵר / טָהוֹר in purity contexts (Lev 11-15; Num 19) — both verbal 'become pure' and adjectival 'pure'.

entries.gloss_en: to appear, manifest oneself, become manifest; (of God) to reveal himself
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for theophanic Hebrew verbs נִרְאָה / וַיֵּרָא when God appears to a patriarch (Gen 17:1 תגלא לה אללה = וַיֵּרָא יהוה אֵלָיו; Gen 48:3). Part of Saadia's anti-anthropomorphic-but-still-personal vocabulary for divine self-disclosure.

entries.gloss_en: to provide for, give sustenance to, supply with livelihood
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew nātan / bērēkh in the recurring Deuteronomic formula 'as YHWH your God has given/blessed you' (כַּאֲשֶׁר נָתַן / בֵּרַךְ → כמא רזקך אללה רבך, Deut 12:7, 12:21).

entries.gloss_en: (impersonal) it will go well (with you); (idiomatic) may you / may things prosper
entries.notes: Form IV passive of kh-y-r 'to be good'. Used impersonally with li- + addressee: yukhāru laka = 'may it go well for you'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for the Deuteronomic formula לְמַעַן יִיטַב לְךָ — rendered לכי יכ'אר לך 'so that it may go well for you' (Deut 12:25, 12:28).

entries.gloss_en: to lie with (sexually), have sexual relations with
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular euphemistic gloss for Hebrew שָׁכַב in sexual contexts (e.g. Gen 26:10 about Abimelech's near-violation of Rebekah; Gen 34:7 about Shechem and Dinah). Form III ḍājaʿa 'to lie with [s.o.]' is the relational sense; Form I ḍajaʿa is just 'to lie down'.

Saadia's regular technical gloss for Hebrew נֵזֶר / נְזִיר / נְזִירוּת — the entire Nazirite pericope at Num 6 uses נסך as the technical term (e.g. אייאם נסכה 'the days of his Naziriteship', Num 6:4). The denominal verb nasaka = 'to be a Nazirite'. technical, in Saadia — Naziriteship.
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew יוֹנָה in offering contexts (especially the formula 'two turtledoves or two young pigeons' תֹּרִים אוֹ בְנֵי יוֹנָה → שפנינין או פרכ'י חמאם, Num 6:10; Gen 15:9).
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מְנוֹרָה — both the seven-branched Tabernacle menorah (Num 8:2-4) and any lampstand. in Saadia — the menorah.

entries.notes: Often used in the partitive sense 'some people' (kāna fīhim unās = 'there were among them some people who...'). Distinct from al-nās (the people in general, the populace).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses unās for the unspecified-plural 'some people / certain men' — e.g. Num 9:6 פכאן פיהם אנאס תנגסו 'there were among them some men who had become defiled'; Gen 47:2 כ'מסה' אנאס מן אכ'ותה 'five of his brothers' (lit. 'five men from his brothers').

entries.gloss_en: burden, load; (figurative) sin, guilt, transgression carried as a burden
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew עֲוֹן in the formula 'and he shall bear his sin' (וְנָשָׂא חֶטְאוֹ / עֲוֹנוֹ → פקד חמל וזרה 'and he has borne his burden/sin' — Num 9:13; Lev 17:16).
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מַבּוּל — the Noahide Flood (Gen 6-11, e.g. Gen 10:1 בנין בעד אלטופאן 'sons after the Flood').

entries.pos: noun (m., here used as sg. 'the Garden')
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew גַּן in Gen 2-3 (the Garden of Eden). Lexically jinān is the plural of janna but is used here in the singular collective sense common in Judeo-Arabic. in Saadia — the Garden of Eden.

entries.notes: Homograph with umma (lemma אמה also) 'nation, community' — root ʔ-m-m, distinct. Context disambiguates: amah always appears in household / personal-possession contexts; umma in nation / people contexts.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew אָמָה (handmaid, female slave) — Sarah's amah Hagar; Rachel's amah Bilhah; the household amah of the Decalogue and tithe-laws (Deut 12:18: ועבדך ואמתך 'your manservant and your maidservant').

entries.gloss_en: young woman, maidservant, slave-girl; (broadly) any girl in service
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew נַעֲרָה (young woman) in narrative — notably for Rebekah's attendant and Rebekah herself before betrothal (Gen 24:28, 24:55), and parallel passages.
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew אַלְמָנָה — usually appearing in the triad 'the stranger, the orphan, and the widow' (אלג'ריב ואליתים ואלארמלה, e.g. Deut 10:18, 14:29).
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew עֲבָדִים in the Exodus-redemption formula 'the house of bondage' (בֵּית עֲבָדִים → בית אלעבודייה, Deut 13:6, 13:11, and parallel passages in Exod and Deut).

entries.gloss_en: Perizzites — one of the seven Canaanite peoples of pre-Israelite Canaan
entries.notes: Frequently paired with אלכנעאניין (Canaanites) — 'and the Canaanites and the Perizzites were then dwelling in the land' (Gen 13:7; 34:30; Deut 7:1).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name; the Arabic-style -iyy- + -īn gentilic plural ending is Saadia's standard for pre-Israelite Canaanite peoples (כנעאניין, פרזיין, אמוריין, חתיין, חויין, יבוסיין, גרגאשיין). Always plural-gentilic in Saadia (the -iyyīn ending).

entries.gloss_en: Mamre — (1) an Amorite ally of Abraham; (2) the oak / grove / plain of Mamre, the patriarchal cult site near Hebron
entries.gloss_he: מַמְרֵא — בעל ברית אברהם והמקום הקרוי על שמו
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged. The locale appears in the formula 'the plain/oak of Mamre' (אֵלוֹנֵי מַמְרֵא → מרג ממרא, e.g. Gen 13:18; 14:13; 18:1; 23:17, 19; 35:27).

entries.gloss_en: Heth — son of Canaan, eponymous ancestor of the Hittites (Gen 10:15); 'sons of Heth' = Hittites (Gen 23 passim)
entries.notes: The gentilic form is אלחתיין (the Hittites).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew form.

entries.gloss_en: Bilhah — Rachel's handmaid (gifted by Laban); mother of Dan and Naphtali
entries.gloss_he: בִּלְהָה, שפחת רחל; אֵם דן ונפתלי
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged.

entries.gloss_en: Hebrew (sg.) — of or pertaining to the Hebrew people; an Israelite
entries.notes: Plural אלעבראניין 'the Hebrews'.
entries.saadia_note: Both forms are Saadia's standard renderings of Hebrew עִבְרִי / עִבְרִים — usually in non-Israelite mouths (Egyptians, Philistines) referring to the patriarchal-Israelite community externally (Gen 14:13 אברם אלעבראני; Gen 39:14, 17; 40:15; 43:32).

entries.gloss_en: to coat, plate, overlay (a surface with metal, paint, pitch); to anoint
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew צִפָּה (overlay with gold/silver) in the Tabernacle construction passages (Exod 26-27; e.g. וטלאהא פצ'ה 'and he overlaid them with silver', Exod 27:10-11).

entries.gloss_en: judge, ruler, magistrate; one who exercises authority
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew שֹׁפֵט in the judicial passages (e.g. Deut 17:9, 17:12: ואלי' אלחאכם אלד'י ילי פי ד'אלך אלזמאן 'and to the judge who is in office in that time').

entries.gloss_en: skilled, expert, accomplished (especially of a craftsman)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew חוֹשֵׁב in the Tabernacle-craftsmanship formulas (e.g. Exod 26:1, 26:31: צנעה' חאד'ק 'the work of a skilled [craftsman]').

entries.gloss_en: fat, suet (of an animal); especially the fat reserved for the altar
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew חֵלֶב — the fat of sacrificial animals that is to be burned on the altar (Lev 3-4, 7; Exod 29; passim). The verb shaḥuma = 'to grow fat'; the adjective shaḥīm = 'fatty'.
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew נִדָּה in the impurity passages (Lev 12; Lev 15; Lev 18; Lev 20) — חיצ'תהא 'her menstruation' (Lev 12:2, 12:5).

entries.notes: Arabic gender polarity: tisʿa (with tā' marbūṭa) counts masculine nouns; tisʿ counts feminine. The form תסעין = 'ninety'.

entries.gloss_en: foreign, outsider, stranger; non-priestly (in cultic contexts)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew זָר in cultic-disqualification contexts — 'an outsider/non-priest who approaches shall be put to death' (Num 1:51, 17:5 — ואי אגנבי תקדם אלי' ד'אלך פליקתל). Distinct from גריב (gharīb) 'stranger, sojourner' which Saadia uses for גֵּר.
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מִזְרָח in directional descriptions — especially the layout of the tribes around the Tabernacle (Num 2:3, 10:5: אלנאזלין פי אלמשרק 'those encamped to the east').
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew בֶּטֶן / רֶחֶם — both anatomical 'belly' and reproductive 'womb'. The phrase כל אוול בטן 'every first-of-the-womb' renders Heb פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם (Num 18:15).

entries.gloss_en: then, thereafter, afterwards (sequential — distinct from fa- 'and then immediately')
entries.notes: The sequential nuance (a clear interval between events) distinguishes it from fa- (immediate consequence) and wa- (mere conjunction).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular sequential conjunction at the head of new narrative units — often glosses Hebrew וַיְהִי-narrative openers (e.g. Num 13:1: תם כלם אללה מוסי' 'Then YHWH spoke to Moses'; Num 20:1; Exod 18:1). Saadia uses tum (תם) rather than the more usual classical thumma (ת'ם, with apos) — scribal/orthographic variation.

entries.gloss_en: Jethro — priest of Midian, father-in-law of Moses
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged.

entries.gloss_en: Eliab — (1) son of Helon, chieftain of Zebulun in the wilderness census; (2) son of Pallu (Reubenite), father of Dathan and Abiram
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged.

entries.gloss_en: Zin — a wilderness south of Canaan, the southernmost section of the Israelite itinerary (Num 13:21; 20:1; 27:14; Deut 32:51)
entries.notes: Distinct from סין (Sin, also a southern wilderness, Exod 16:1; 17:1).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains both Hebrew forms unchanged.

entries.gloss_en: Hittites — one of the seven Canaanite peoples; descendants of Heth son of Canaan
entries.notes: Frequently appears in the seven-nation list (Exod 13:5; Num 13:29; Deut 7:1).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name and uses the standard Arabic-style gentilic plural — see also כנעאניין, פרזיין, אמוריין, חויין, יבוסיין, גרגאשיין. Always plural-gentilic in Saadia (the -iyyīn ending).

entries.gloss_en: shore, bank (of a river, sea, or wadi)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew שָׂפָה / גְּדָה when describing the bank of a river, sea, or wadi (e.g. Num 13:29: עלי שאט אלארדון 'on the bank of the Jordan'; Gen 22:17: עלי' שאט אלבחר 'on the seashore').

entries.gloss_en: child, infant, young one (esp. of human children); pl. aṭfāl = 'the little ones'
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew טַף (collective 'the little ones, dependents') throughout the Exodus and Numbers narratives (e.g. Num 14:31: ואטפאלכם 'and your little ones').

entries.gloss_en: to be able, to have the power/capacity to (something)
entries.notes: Distinct from the existing entry taʾiq-able (lemma טאיק), which is the active participle ṭāʾiq 'able [adj.]'. This is the finite-verb form. Often paired with an + verb: 'he was able to + INF'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew יָכֹל in narrative — e.g. Num 14:16 ממא לם יטיק 'because he was not able'; Gen 36:7 ולם יטיק בלד 'and the land was not able [to support them]'.

entries.gloss_en: behind, after; following (after); on the far side of
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses warāʾ both spatially ('behind' — Num 3:23 ינזלון ורא אלמסכן 'they encamp behind the tabernacle') and as 'after' a person ('Joseph went after his brothers' Gen 37:17). In the figurative sense it renders Hebrew אַחֲרֵי of straying after one's heart (Num 15:39 טאג'יון וראהם 'wandering after them').

entries.gloss_en: to burn (as incense or sacrifice — sending smoke/aroma up); to fumigate, send up in smoke
entries.notes: Form II (قَتَّر) of q-t-r. Imperative wa-qattir = 'and burn (it) up in smoke'. Cognate with Hebrew הִקְטִיר (hifʿil of q-ṭ-r).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew הִקְטִיר in priestly contexts — the verb covers both burning of the fat on the altar (Num 18:17: וקתר שחמהא 'and burn its fat in smoke') and burning of incense generally (Exod 29:13). The Hebrew and Arabic share the same triliteral root q-ṭ-r.

entries.gloss_en: to sprinkle, spatter (liquid — water, blood, oil — onto a surface or person)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew הִזָּה in purification rites — sprinkling of the red-heifer waters (Num 19), of blood in atonement (Lev 4-5), of oil at consecration (Lev 14:7). The blue-fringes formula 'sprinkle with the water of impurity' and the leper's seven sprinklings both use וינצ'ח.
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew כֶּרֶם (the Hebrew and Arabic words share the root k-r-m). Appears in property-rights and refusal-of-passage passages (Num 16:14; 20:17).

entries.gloss_en: mouth (of a person, animal, or an opening — pit, cave, sack)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew פֶּה — both anatomical ('the ground opened its mouth', Num 16:30, 16:32) and metaphorical ('the mouth of the sack', etc.). The classical form is fam (فم); the Quranic / poetic / Saadianic form fā (with construct status changes — fū / fā / fī) is used freely in Judeo-Arabic.

entries.notes: Homograph with barr-wilderness (lemma בר, root b-r-r, sense 'wilderness'). Context disambiguates: burr always appears in food / offering contexts, barr in geographic ones.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מִנְחָה in the offering formulas — וברהם ומזאגהם 'their grain-offering and their drink-offering' (Num 29:18 ff., parallel to סֹלֶת). The wheat sense is also used directly for Hebrew דָּגָן / קָמַח in non-cultic passages. in Saadia's sacrificial vocabulary — the grain offering / minḥah.
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מוּם — the technical term for the sacrificial-animal blemishes that disqualify an offering (Num 19:2; Deut 15:21; Lev 22; Lev 21 for priests).

entries.gloss_en: running, flowing (of water — a spring, a fresh source); the act of welling up
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מַיִם חַיִּים ('running / living water') in purification passages (Num 19:17: מא נביע פי אנא 'running water in a vessel'; Lev 14; Lev 15). The phrase מן נביע דמהא 'from the flow of her blood' renders Heb מִמְּקוֹר דָּמֶיהָ (Lev 12:7).

entries.gloss_en: north; the northern direction; (sometimes) left hand
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew צָפוֹן in directional descriptions — especially the layout of the tribes (Num 2:25 פי אלשמאל 'in the north') and the Levitical encampment (Num 3:35).

entries.notes: Form III passive participle of b-r-k. Active form mubārik = 'one who blesses'; passive mubārak = 'the one blessed'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew בָּרוּךְ as a stative ascription — most famously the Balaam-pericope formula מן תבארכה מבארך 'whom you bless is blessed' (Num 22:6, 22:12).

entries.gloss_en: wagon, cart (wheeled vehicle for carrying loads); (broader) any wheeled conveyance
entries.notes: Cognate with Hebrew עֲגָלָה — both languages use the same root ʿ-j-l ('haste / round, rolling'). Distinct from ʿijl 'calf' (also ʿ-j-l).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew עֲגָלָה — the carts donated by the tribal chiefs at the Tabernacle dedication (Num 7:3-8: אלעגל ואלבקר 'the carts and the cattle') and the wagons Joseph sent to fetch Jacob (Gen 45:19, 27; 46:5).

entries.gloss_en: Abiram — son of Eliab (Reubenite), co-conspirator with Korah and Dathan in the rebellion against Moses (Num 16; 26:9; Deut 11:6)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged. Almost always appears in the pair דתן ואבירם.

entries.gloss_en: Peor — (1) the Moabite deity Baal-Peor; (2) the mountain/place of his worship in the plains of Moab (Num 23:28; 25:3, 5, 18; 31:16; Deut 4:3)
entries.gloss_he: פְּעוֹר — בעל פעור והמקום הקרוי על שמו
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name. Often follows ל or פעור אלצנם ('Peor the idol').

entries.gloss_en: Hivites — one of the seven Canaanite peoples; descendants of Hivvi son of Canaan (Gen 10:17)
entries.notes: Frequently appears in the seven-nation list (Exod 13:5; Deut 7:1; Deut 20:17; Gen 10:17).
entries.saadia_note: Always plural-gentilic in Saadia (the -iyyīn ending).

entries.gloss_en: Gomorrah — the Cities-of-the-Plain that YHWH destroyed alongside Sodom (Gen 10:19; 13:10; 14:2, 8, 10-11; 18:20; 19:24, 28; Deut 29:23; 32:32)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged. Always paired with סדום (Sodom).

entries.gloss_en: Nahor — (1) Abraham's grandfather (Gen 11:22-25); (2) Abraham's brother, husband of Milcah (Gen 11:26-29; 22:20-23; 24:10, 15, 24, 47)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged.

entries.gloss_en: young of a bird, fledgling, chick; pl. firākh = 'young pigeons'
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew בֶּן (in the offering formula 'a young pigeon' בֶּן יוֹנָה → פרך' חמאם, Num 6:10; Lev 12:8; Gen 15:9). Always paired with חמאם 'pigeons'.

entries.gloss_en: (1) a good deed, merit, righteous act; (2) beautiful (fem.sg. of ḥasan)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew צְדָקָה in the merit sense (Gen 15:6: וכתבהא לה חסנה 'and he counted it to him as a meritorious deed' = וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ לּוֹ צְדָקָה). In construct-state usage חסנה' אלמנצ'ר 'beautiful of appearance' renders Heb יְפַת מַרְאֶה (Gen 12:11; 24:16).

entries.gloss_en: appearance, sight, look, view; that which is seen
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מַרְאֶה in the recurring formula 'beautiful in appearance' (יְפַת מַרְאֶה → חסנה' אלמנצ'ר; Gen 12:11; 24:16; 29:17, etc.).

entries.notes: Homograph with ʿagalah/ʿagal 'wagon, cart' (same root ʿ-j-l). Context disambiguates: ʿijl is always animate, the offspring or young of cattle.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew עֵגֶל (calf) in non-cultic narrative — e.g. Abraham's hospitality (Gen 18:7 עגלא רכ'צ'א וטייבא 'a tender, good calf'); Gen 15:9 (Covenant of the Pieces). Saadia uses it for Hebrew עֵגֶל.

entries.gloss_en: little, few; a small amount, a bit (of)
entries.notes: Often used adverbially: قَلِيلًا (qalīlan) = 'a little, slightly'. Distinct from kathīr 'much, many'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מְעַט — 'a little water' (Gen 18:4 קליל מן מא; Gen 24:17 קליל מאא = מְעַט מַיִם).

entries.notes: Homograph with am-or-particle (lemma אם, the disjunctive 'or'). Context disambiguates: 'mother' always with possessive suffix or as construct head, 'or' as a sentence-medial particle.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew אֵם — the matriarchs, the mother-of-a-house, and the recurring 'his mother' / 'your mother' formulas.
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew בֵּית הַסֹּהַר in the Joseph narrative (Gen 39:20-23; 40 passim — אלסגן 'the prison'; רייס אלסגן 'the warden of the prison').

Saadia uses both مكان (mawḍiʿ-like) and موضع interchangeably for Hebrew מָקוֹם. The adverbial 'a place for X' (Deut 1:33 ליצלח לכם מכאנא לנזולכם 'to prepare for you a place for your encampment'; Exod 25:27) takes the accusative-indefinite. The full-form synonym of moḍiʿ (موضع) which Saadia uses more often in the Pentateuch for Heb מָקוֹם.

entries.notes: Masculine collective. Distinct from baqara (lemma בקרה, fem.sg.) 'cow'.
