entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew בָּקָר collectively — including in the recurring 'your cattle and your flock' (בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנְךָ → בקרך וג'נמך, Deut 12:17, 12:21, 14:23, etc.). Saadia uses bāqar / al-baqar for the collective Heb בָּקָר and baqara for the individual cow.

Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew יָתוֹם — always in the protected-classes triad 'the stranger, the orphan, and the widow' (אלג'ריב ואליתים ואלארמלה: Deut 10:18; 14:29; 16:11; 16:14; 24:17-21; 26:12-13; 27:19).

entries.gloss_en: free, free-born; (as noun) a free person; (in manumission contexts) freed
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew חָפְשִׁי in the slave-release passages (Deut 15:12-13: אטלקה חרא 'release him as a freedman'; Exod 21:2, 5).

entries.gloss_en: to fall, drop down; to happen, occur, befall; (with ʿalā) to come upon, descend on
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew נָפַל both literally (Gen 15:12 וקע סבאת עלי' אברם 'a deep sleep fell upon Abram'; Num 14:5 פוקע מוסי' והרון 'Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces') and idiomatically (וקע וגהך 'your face has fallen' = Gen 4:6).

entries.gloss_en: to beware, take care, guard oneself (against); (imperative) iḥdhar = 'beware! take care!'
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew הִשָּׁמֶר 'beware!' in admonitions (Gen 24:6 אחד'ר אן תרד אבני 'beware that you not take my son back'; Gen 31:24 אחד'ר אן תכלם יעקב 'beware that you not speak to Jacob anything from good to bad').

entries.gloss_en: to turn aside, deviate, swerve; to depart from
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew סוּר (in 'turn aside from' the way / from the commandment) — especially Deut 17:11, 17:20, 28:14: לא תזול מן אלאמר 'do not turn aside from the commandment'.

entries.gloss_en: to bless, invoke blessing on; (with ʿalā or fī) to bless [s.o.]
entries.notes: Form III bāraka 'to bless' — passive participle mubārak 'blessed' is already in the dict.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew בֵּרֵךְ — God blessing the patriarchs (Gen 28:3 יבארך עליך 'he will bless you'; Gen 48:16 יבארך פי הד'ין אלג'לאמין 'may he bless these two lads'); the priestly blessing (Num 6:24).

entries.gloss_en: 'here I am!', 'at your service!', 'I am listening' — the formulaic response to a call
entries.notes: Originally the dual of labb 'one who responds positively/repeatedly'; later frozen as a formulaic response. Used in pilgrimage formulas and in conversational responses.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew הִנֵּנִי when used as a response to being called by name — the Akedah dialogue (Gen 22:1, 22:7, 22:11), Jacob (Gen 31:11), Moses (Exod 3:4), Samuel (1 Sam 3:4).

entries.gloss_en: Zoar — one of the Cities-of-the-Plain; Lot's refuge after the destruction of Sodom (Gen 13:10; 14:2, 8; 19:22-23, 30; Deut 34:3)
entries.notes: Originally Bela (Gen 14:2, 8); renamed Zoar after Lot's refuge. The Arabic-Hebrew correspondence ZGR↔ZOR uses ghain (ג') for the Hebrew ʿayin sound.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name. The form זג'ר reflects the standard rendering of Hebrew ʿayin into Arabic via ghain (غ).

entries.gloss_en: Hanoch / Enoch — (1) son of Cain (Gen 4:17-18); (2) son of Jared (Gen 5:18-24), 'who walked with God'; (3) son of Reuben (Gen 46:9; Num 26:5); (4) grandson of Abraham via Midian (Gen 25:4)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged. Used for all four scripturally-distinct figures of the same name.

entries.gloss_en: to keep, guard, preserve, watch over; (with abstract object) to observe (a commandment, a covenant)
entries.notes: JA scribal convention varies: trailing ẓād may be written חפז (no apos), חפצ (apos absent, ṣād-style), or חפצ' (with apos marking ẓ). Variants list collapses all three.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew שָׁמַר in covenantal / mitzvah contexts — 'and you shall keep' (Deut 5:29: ואחפצו; Exod 12:17: ואחפצו אלפטיר 'and you shall keep the unleavened bread').

entries.gloss_en: to bring out, lead forth, cause to come out (transitive — Form IV of kharaja 'to go out')
entries.notes: Form IV (أَخْرَج). Distinct from the existing kharaja-exit which is Form I (intransitive 'to go out').
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew הוֹצִיא — the Exodus formula 'who brought you out from the land of Egypt' (אלמכ'רגכם מן בלד מצר). The 1cs perfect אכ'רגתהם 'I brought them out' appears in Deut 9:12, 9:29.

entries.gloss_en: to declare ritually clean / pronounce pure (Form II ṭahhara, transitive — distinct from Form I 'to be pure'); (passive ptcp) the one who is being declared clean
entries.notes: Form II (طَهَّر) of ṭ-h-r — declarative/causative 'to declare s.o. clean'. Distinct from the Form I tahara 'to be / become pure'. The active ptcp muṭahhir = 'the one who declares clean'; passive ptcp muṭahhar / muṭṭahhir = 'the one being purified'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew טִהֵר (pi'el) — the priest's declarative act of pronouncing a leprosy patient clean (Lev 13:6, 13:13, 13:17, 13:23, 13:28 — פליטהרה 'let him declare him clean'; Lev 14:7 ויטהרה).

entries.gloss_en: to accept, approve, find acceptable (passive yurtaḍā = 'it is accepted/approved')
entries.notes: Form VIII (اِرْتَضَى) of r-ḍ-y. Distinct from the Form-I raḍiya 'to be pleased' and Form-II raḍḍā 'to please'. The passive yurtaḍā renders 'it is approved/accepted'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for the Hebrew technical formula 'it shall be accepted / for acceptance' (לִרְצֹנוֹ / יֵרָצֶה → ירתצ'א ענה / ירתצ'א מנכם 'it is accepted on his behalf / accepted from you', Lev 1:3, 19:5, 22:25, 22:27).

entries.gloss_en: to requite, recompense, reward; (with 1cs subject) 'I will reward / repay'
entries.notes: Form III jāzā (جَازَى) of j-z-y. The 1cs imperfect ujāzī takes a direct object (ujāzīkum 'I reward you') often with khayran ('with good') as the cognate complement.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew אֲנִי יְהוָה / שָׁמַרְתֶּם וַעֲשִׂיתֶם וְאֶהְיֶה formulas of divine reward — 'I am YHWH your God who rewards you with good' (Lev 18:4, 18:30, 19:37, 25:55: אנא אללה רבכם אגאזיכם כ'ירא). The cognate noun jazāʾ = 'reward, requital'.

entries.gloss_en: produce, yield, crop, harvest-revenue (of a field, vineyard, orchard)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew תְּבוּאָה in the agricultural-cycle passages (Exod 23:10, Lev 25:3: ותגמע ג'לתהא 'and gather in its produce').

entries.gloss_en: molding, decorative rim (a raised border running around the edge of a flat surface)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew זֵר ('a golden rim/border') in the Tabernacle furniture passages — the rim around the Ark, the table, the altar (Exod 25:11 'a molding of gold around it' = זיגא מן ד'הב מסתדירא; 25:24-25; 30:3-4; 37:2, 11, 26).

entries.gloss_en: carrying-poles, staves (the wooden bars used to carry the Ark, the Table, and the Altar)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew בַּדִּים in the Tabernacle-construction passages (Exod 25:13-15, 26-28; 27:6-7; 30:4-5; 37:4-5, 14-15, 27-28; 38:5-7; 40:20 — אדכ'ל אלדהוק פי אלחלק 'put the staves into the rings').

entries.notes: The Arabic-form 'one' — distinct from the Hebrew form אחד (already in dict).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew אֶחָד / אַחַת — the femminine ואחדה / אלואחדה appears repeatedly in the Tabernacle dimensions (Exod 26 passim — אלשקה אלואחדה 'the one curtain'). Numerical 'one and the other' / 'one of them' collocations also use this stem. Saadia uses wāḥid in his Arabic prose; the Hebrew form אחד appears mainly in the Shemaʿ (Deut 6:4: אללה רבנא אללה ואחד 'YHWH our God, YHWH is one') and other Hebraisms.

entries.gloss_en: loop, hook-loop, eyelet (especially of cloth, for fastening)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew לֻלָאֹת ('loops') in the Tabernacle-curtain passages — 'fifty loops on each curtain' (Exod 26:4-11; 36:11-17 — כ'מסין ערוה).

entries.gloss_en: corner, pillar, support; (in Tabernacle architecture) the corner-projection of the altar
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew קֶרֶן in the altar-corner-projection sense ('horns' of the altar) — Exod 27:2, 30:2 ואצנע ארכאנה עלי' ארבע גהאתה 'make its corners on its four sides'; Exod 30:10; Lev 4 passim.

entries.gloss_en: caul, the fatty membrane covering the entrails (especially the omentum)
entries.gloss_he: חֵלֶב הַמְכַסֶּה אֶת הַקֶּרֶב, יוֹתֶרֶת הַכָּבֵד
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew חֵלֶב הַמְכַסֶּה אֶת הַקֶּרֶב — the fatty caul over the inner organs of a sacrificial animal (Exod 29:13, 22; Lev 3:3, 9, 14; Lev 4:8 — אלת'רב אלמג'טי אלגוף 'the caul that covers the entrails').

entries.gloss_en: thumb (of the hand); big toe (of the foot)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew בֹּהֶן — both 'thumb of the right hand' and 'big toe of the right foot' in the consecration of priests (Exod 29:20: עלי' אבהאם אידיהם אלאיאמין) and the cleansing of the leper (Lev 14:14, 14:17, 14:25, 14:28).

Saadia's regular technical gloss for Hebrew מִלּוּאִים ('ordination-installment') in the priestly-consecration passages (Exod 29:22, 26, 27, 31, 34: כבש אלכמאל 'the ram of the ordination'; Lev 8:22, 28-29, 31, 33). The Hebrew מילוי 'filling [of the hand]' and Arabic kamāl 'completion' are conceptually parallel. technical, in Saadia — the ordination / consecration installment-offering.

entries.gloss_en: stand, base, seat, pedestal (the supporting base of a vessel)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew כֵּן ('stand, base') of the laver (Exod 30:18; 30:28; 31:9; 35:16; 38:8; 39:39; 40:11; Lev 8:11 — אלחוץ' ומקעדה 'the laver and its stand').
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew לָבָן (the color, not the personal name). Most prominent in the leprosy-diagnosis passages (Lev 13 passim — אביצ'א 'white', בקעה ביצ'א 'a white spot').

entries.gloss_en: nakedness, pudenda; that which it is shameful to expose
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular euphemistic gloss for Hebrew עֶרְוָה in the forbidden-relations chapter (Lev 18; Lev 20). Form: 'do not uncover the pudenda of X' = לא תכשף סוות X (Lev 18:7-19; Deut 27:20). idiomatic, in Saadia — the genital sphere of a forbidden relative.

entries.gloss_en: solid, of one piece, hammered/turned out from a single mass (not assembled)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מִקְשָׁה — describing the construction of the silver trumpets (Num 10:2: מן פצה מצמתה 'of solid silver') and the menorah (Num 8:4: והד'ה צנעה' אלמנארה מצמתה ד'הב 'and this is the workmanship of the lampstand — solid gold'; Exod 25:18, 31, 36; 37:7, 17, 22).

Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew דֶּגֶל ('standard, tribal-division banner') in the encampment-layout passages (Num 2 passim, Num 10:14-25 — מרכז עסכר X 'the central encampment of the troop of X'). in Saadia — the central / leading encampment of a tribal division.

entries.gloss_en: Ammihud — father of Elishama (chieftain of Ephraim in the wilderness census; Num 1:10; 2:18; 7:48, 53; 10:22)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged.

entries.gloss_en: Enan — father of Ahira (chieftain of Naphtali in the wilderness census; Num 1:15; 2:29; 7:78, 83; 10:27)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged.

entries.gloss_en: Paran — the wilderness south of Canaan and east of the Sinai peninsula; major staging-point for the Israelite itinerary (Num 10:12; 12:16; 13:3, 26; Gen 21:21; Deut 1:1; 33:2; 1 Sam 25:1; Hab 3:3)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged.

entries.gloss_en: Reuel — (1) son of Esau and Basemath (Gen 36:4, 10, 13, 17; 1 Chr 1:35, 37); (2) Midianite priest, father-in-law of Moses (Exod 2:18; Num 10:29); (3) father of Eliasaph the Gadite chieftain (Num 2:14)
entries.notes: Sometimes identified with Jethro / Hobab (Num 10:29 names Reuel as the father of Hobab the father-in-law of Moses; Exod 2:18 names Reuel directly as Moses' father-in-law).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged.

entries.gloss_en: better, more beneficial, more advantageous, the best choice
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew טוֹב לָנוּ ('better for us') in the wilderness-rebellion grumbling formulas (Num 11:18 וכאן אלאצלח לנא במצר 'and it was better for us in Egypt'; Num 14:3 אלאצלח לנא אלרגוע אלי' מצר 'better for us to return to Egypt').

entries.gloss_en: (1) sharp, keen (of eyes, perception); (2) iron (as noun)
entries.notes: The adjectival sense 'sharp / keen-of-sight' translates Heb שְׁתֻם הָעָיִן in Balaam's oracle; the nominal sense 'iron' appears in weapons contexts.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses חדיד אלבצר 'keen-of-sight' for Hebrew שְׁתֻם הָעָיִן in Balaam's third and fourth oracles (Num 24:3, 24:15 — אלרגל אלחדיד אלבצר 'the man with the keen sight'). The 'iron' sense surfaces in homicide-by-iron-weapon passages (Num 35:16 בְאֶבֶן יָד 'with an iron implement').

entries.gloss_en: to perish, die (violently or by judgment); to be destroyed
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew הִכָּרֵת / אָבַד / סָפָה in judgment contexts — 'lest they perish' (Num 17:25, 18:3 — לא יהלכון; Deut 4:26).

entries.gloss_en: to be cut off, severed, terminated; (in karet contexts) to be excised from the community
entries.notes: Form VII (passive-reflexive) of q-ṭ-ʿ. The Form-I qataʿa 'he cut' is transitive; Form VII inqataʿa is the result-state.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew הִכָּרֵת (the karet penalty 'cut off') in covenant-violation contexts — Num 15:31 פינקטע ד'אלך אלאנסאן 'and that person shall be cut off'; Num 19:20.

entries.gloss_en: to lift, raise, elevate; to take up (an offering)
entries.notes: Form-I cognate of the existing marfu-raised (passive participle). Form VIII irtafaʿa = 'to rise up'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew הֵרִים / נָשָׂא in physical-lifting and offering-elevation contexts — 'he lifted his hand' (Num 20:11 פרפע ידה), 'Moses brought their case before YHWH' (Num 27:5 פרפע מוסי' חכמהן), 'he shall take up an offering' (Num 18:24 ירפעוהא; Lev 7).

entries.gloss_en: to rise up, ascend, be raised up, be lifted
entries.notes: Form VIII (اِرْتَفَع) of r-f-ʿ. Used both literally ('the cloud lifted/ascended') and figuratively ('the divine glory was lifted').
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew נֶעֱלָה / הֵעָלָה — most prominently for the cloud lifting from over the Tabernacle and the people setting out (Num 9:21-22, Num 10:11 — ירתפע אלג'מאם 'the cloud lifts up'). Also: 'and YHWH's light was lifted from Abraham' (Gen 17:22, 18:33 — ארתפע נור אללה ען אברהים).

entries.gloss_en: to cover, blanket, conceal (with a covering)
entries.notes: Form II (غَطَّى). The active ptcp mughaṭṭi 'covering' and passive ptcp mughaṭṭā 'covered' both appear.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew כִּסָּה — most notably in Balak's complaint about Israel 'covering the face of the land' (Num 22:5, 22:11 — קד ג'טא צ'אהר אלארץ' 'has covered the face of the land'). Also the technical 'the caul that covers the entrails' (אלת'רב אלמג'טי אלגוף, Lev 3:3 etc.).

entries.gloss_en: to alight, descend, settle (upon); to come to rest in a place; (idiomatic) to befall, come upon
entries.notes: Form I of ḥ-l-l. The Form-IV causative ahalla 'to cause to alight' is already in the dict.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew הָיְתָה עָלָיו ('it came upon him') in prophetic-spirit contexts — Num 24:2: חלת עלי'ה נבווה' אללה 'the prophecy of God alighted upon him'; Deut 2:15: חלת בהם 'it [the hand of YHWH] came upon them'.

Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מַכָּה — both the literal blow (Num 35:16 צ'רבה באנא חדיד 'a blow with an iron implement') and the divine plague-strike (Num 11:33 פצ'רבהם צ'רבה עצ'ימה גדא 'he struck them with a very great blow'). in Saadia — a plague-strike.

Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew חֲלוֹם in prophetic-revelation contexts ('I speak to him in a dream', Num 12:6 כ'אטבתה פי חלם; Gen 20:3 פי חלם אלליל 'in the dream of the night') and in narrative (Joseph and Pharaoh's dreams, Gen 37, 40-41).

entries.gloss_en: portion, share, lot (of inheritance, of spoils, of one's allotment)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew חֵלֶק in inheritance and apportionment contexts — 'you shall have no portion among them' (Num 18:20 ולא יכון לך נציב פי מא בינהם; Deut 10:9, 12:12, 14:27, 14:29, 18:1). Also for war-spoils apportionment (Num 31).

entries.gloss_en: group, troop, division, party; band of people
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew אִישׁ עַל-דִּגְלוֹ / אִישׁ עַל-מַחֲנֵהוּ ('each by his standard') and similar group-designations in the encampment passages (Num 2:17 כל פריק פי מכאנה 'each group in its place'; Num 4:19 כל פריק עלי כ'דמתה 'each group to its task').

entries.gloss_en: facing, toward, in front of, to meet (with motion-verbs of meeting/intercepting)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew לִקְרַאת ('toward, to meet') in meeting-narratives — 'Edom came out toward them' (Num 20:20 פכ'רג אדום תלקאהם; Num 21:23; 22:36; Gen 14:17; 24:17; 32:7).

Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew תֶּבֶן — fodder for camels (Gen 24:25, 32 — ואעטא תבנא וקתא לאלגמאל 'and he gave straw and provender to the camels') and the recurring 'straw is given' in the Exodus brick-making formula (Exod 5).

entries.gloss_en: Miriam — sister of Moses and Aaron, prophetess and leader of the women's song at the Sea (Exod 15:20-21; Num 12; 20:1; 26:59)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged.

entries.gloss_en: Hebron — the patriarchal city; site of Machpelah and Mamre (Gen 13:18; 23:2, 19; 35:27; 37:14; Num 13:22; Josh 14-15)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's standard form for Hebrew חֶבְרוֹן. The variant חברון also appears. Saadia uses the form חברא (without the final ון suffix) — the Aramaic-style truncation rather than the Hebrew construct.

Saadia uses āya for Hebrew אוֹת (sign, miraculous portent) — the signs of Moses (Exod 4; Num 14:11, 14:22). The form אייה' (with trailing apos) is the construct. in Quranic and Saadianic usage — a scriptural verse, a wonder.

entries.gloss_en: to live, be alive, come to life
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew חַי / חָיָה in the live-or-die formulas — 'oh that Ishmael might live before you' (Gen 17:18 לית אסמאעיל יחיא); 'woe to the one who lives' (Num 24:23).

entries.gloss_en: to tie, bind, knot, contract; (figuratively) to make a binding agreement, vow
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew אָסַר אִסָּר in the vows pericope (Num 30: עקד עקודהא 'she has bound her bindings'). The cognate noun ʿaqd / ʿuqūd = 'contract, knot, binding-vow'.

entries.gloss_en: to perish, come to an end, be consumed, be exhausted; to die out
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew תָּם / כָּלָה in extinction-formulas — 'until all that generation died out' (Num 32:13 אלי' אן פני גמיע אלגיל; Deut 2:14-15); 'the money ran out' (Gen 47:15 פני אלורק 'the silver was exhausted').

entries.gloss_en: to be complete, be finished, come to fullness; (with subject = 'days') to be fulfilled (of a period of time)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew וַיְכֻלּוּ / וַתִּמְלָאוּ — 'the heavens and earth were completed' (Gen 2:1 כמלת אלסמאואת); 'her days to give birth were fulfilled' (Gen 25:24 ולמא כמלת איאם ולאדהא). Cognate noun kamāl is in the separate kamal-completion entry.

entries.gloss_en: to bury (a corpse), inter; to conceal in the ground
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew קָבַר in the burial-narratives — Abraham burying Sarah (Gen 23:4-19 אדפן מייתי 'that I may bury my dead'); the patriarchal burials at Machpelah; Joseph's burial requests (Gen 50).

entries.gloss_en: livestock, cattle (the animals that 'walk', as opposed to fixed property)
entries.notes: Plural mawāshī (מואשי).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מִקְנֶה in property-and-livestock contexts (Num 32:1, 4: ומאשיה כת'ירה 'and great livestock'; Gen 46:32; 47:6; Exod 12:38).

entries.gloss_en: (1) shepherds (plural of rāʿī); (2) to pasture, tend a flock (as verb)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew רוֹעִים in pastoral narratives — 'a dispute arose between the herdsmen of Abram and the herdsmen of Lot' (Gen 13:7 בין רעא מאשיה' אברם), 'the shepherds gathered' (Gen 29:3, 8).

entries.gloss_en: protected enclosure, sanctuary, refuge; an asylum-area
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew עִיר מִקְלָט ('city of refuge') — Num 35:11-15, Deut 19:1-13 (קרא חמא 'cities of refuge'; קרי' אלחמא).

Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew לְהָאִיר in the luminary-creation and lampstand-oil passages — 'a luminary for illumination by day' (Gen 1:16 לאלאצ'אה פי אלנהאר); 'oil for the lighting' (Exod 25:6; 27:20; 35:14; Lev 24:2). in Saadia — the act of lighting the lamps / luminaries.

entries.gloss_en: width, breadth; (geometrically) the lateral dimension (paired with ṭūl 'length')
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew רֹחַב in measurement passages — both Tabernacle dimensions (Exod 26:2 וערצ'הא ארבעה' אד'רע) and land-extent ('walk through the land its length and width' Gen 13:17 טולהא וערצ'הא).

entries.gloss_en: tree, plant, shrub (with a woody stem)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew עֵץ (both singular tree and collective). Frequent in narrative ('rest under the tree' Gen 18:4, 8 תחת אלשגרה) and theological-symbolic ('the tree of life, the tree of knowledge of good and evil' Gen 2:9 — שגרה' אלחיאה / שגרה' מערפה' אלכ'יר ואלשר).

entries.gloss_en: facing, opposite, in front of, across-from
entries.saadia_note: Synonym of ḥidhāʾ (חד'א, also 'facing') — Saadia uses both, sometimes interchangeably.

Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew גָּמָל — the camels in Rebekah's betrothal narrative (Gen 24 passim — אלגמאל 'the camels'), Jacob and Laban (Gen 31), and the levitical animal-clean/unclean lists (Lev 11:4; Deut 14:7).

entries.gloss_en: Machir — son of Manasseh, ancestor of the Machirite clan and of Gilead (Gen 50:23; Num 26:29; 27:1; 32:39-40; 36:1; Deut 3:15; Josh 13:31; 17:1)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged. The gentilic 'Machirites' = אלמכיריין.

entries.gloss_en: Haran — (1) Abraham's brother, father of Lot, Milcah, Iscah (Gen 11:27-29); (2) Aramean city in upper Mesopotamia, Abraham's intermediate dwelling-place (Gen 11:31-12:5; 27:43; 28:10; 29:4)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged for both senses (person and place).

entries.gloss_en: to drink, sip, imbibe; (with min) to drink of
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew שָׁתָה — the daily-life verb and the cultic 'libation' contexts. Imperative ishrab = 'drink!' (Gen 24:14, 18, 46 — Rebekah at the well).

entries.gloss_en: to return; (idiomatic with adjective-complement) 'to be still / yet [in a state]' (hal ʿāda X bāqī = 'is X still alive?')
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew הַעוֹדֶנּוּ / עוֹד in the recurring formula 'is your father still alive?' (Gen 43:7, 27, 28; 45:3, 26, 28 — הל עאד אביכם באקי 'is your father still surviving'). Also used in narrative 'returning' senses.

entries.gloss_en: to fear, be afraid (of); (idiomatic) 'fear not!' lā takhaf
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew יָרֵא — both 'fear of God' and 'fear of harm'. The recurring oracle formula 'fear not!' renders Heb אַל-תִּירָא (לא תכ'אפ; pl. לא תכ'אפו, Gen 43:23; 50:19, 21).

entries.gloss_en: to walk, go, travel, journey; (with bayn yaday) to go before / lead the way
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew הָלַךְ in the recurring 'YHWH (or his light) walks before you' formula (Deut 31:3 נורה יסיר בין ידיך; Exod 32:1 יסיר בין ידינא; Num 14:14). Also 'walk in his ways' (Deut 10:12 תסיר פי טרקה).

Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מַצֵּבָה — Jacob's pillar at Bethel (Gen 28:18, 22 — וגעלהא דכה 'and he made it a pillar'; 31:13, 45-52; 35:14, 20). Note: this is the cultic/memorial 'standing stone', distinct from the polytheistic מַצֵּבָה condemned in the Deuteronomic legislation. in Saadia — a standing-stone monument, pillar.

entries.gloss_en: (1) ear (anatomical); (2) particle idhan = 'truly, indeed, in fact; therefore, in that case'
entries.notes: The two senses share the same surface but are etymologically distinct (ʔ-dh-n 'ear' vs. the particle idhan from ʔ-dh-n 'permission/then'). Context disambiguates.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses אד'ן in both senses: (1) anatomical ear in the priestly consecration and leper-purification rites (Exod 29:20 שחמה' אד'ן הרון 'the lobe of Aaron's ear'; Lev 14:14); (2) the truly/indeed particle at sudden realization (Gen 28:16 אד'ן נור אללה פי הד'א אלמוצ'ע 'truly YHWH's light is in this place' = אָכֵן יֵשׁ יְהוָה בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה).

entries.gloss_en: seal, signet, signet-ring (used both as personal authentication and as an engraving tool)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew חוֹתָם / חוֹתֶמֶת — Judah's signet given as Tamar's pledge (Gen 38:18, 25 הד'א אלכ'אתם); the engraving of priestly-breastplate names (Exod 28:11, 21, 36; 39:6, 14, 30: כנקש אלכ'אתם 'like the engraving of a seal').

entries.gloss_en: spirit, soul, breath; vital principle; (in theological contexts) the divine spirit
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew רוּחַ — both the divine 'spirit of God' (Gen 41:38 רוח אללה; Num 11:17, 25, 26, 29; Num 24:2) and the human-vital 'spirit revived' (Gen 45:27 פעאשת רוח יעקוב). Saadia uses different lexical strategies for רוח-as-wind (typically ריח) and רוח-as-spirit (רוח).

entries.gloss_en: silver (especially as currency, minted silver coinage)
entries.notes: Distinct from the noun fiḍḍa (פצ'ה) 'silver' as a metal — wariq specifically denotes coined / monetary silver.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew כֶּסֶף in monetary contexts (currency for the famine, slave-purchases, indemnities) — Gen 47:14-15: אלורק 'the silver', 'until the silver ran out' (פני אלורק). Saadia uses fiḍḍa (פצ'ה) for non-monetary silver (Tabernacle utensils, raw metal).

entries.gloss_en: cloven hoof (of ruminants — sheep, goat, cattle)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew פַּרְסָה in the clean-animal criteria of Lev 11 and Deut 14:6-8 — מצ'לפה בצ'לף 'cleft-hoofed in its hoof'.

entries.gloss_en: rumination, chewing the cud (of ruminant animals)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew גֵּרָה in the clean-animal criteria (Lev 11; Deut 14:6-7) — מצעדה אגתראר 'bringing up the cud'. The verbal form ijtarra = 'to ruminate, chew the cud'; the active ptcp mujtirr.

entries.gloss_en: leaven, leavened bread; (broader) anything that has fermented
entries.notes: Distinct from khamr 'wine' (also kh-m-r). The Passover-leaven prohibition uses khamīr; the wine sense uses khamr.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew חָמֵץ in the Passover prohibitions (Exod 12:15, 19, 20; Exod 13:7; Lev 2:11; Deut 16:3-4 — ולא ירא לך כ'מיר 'and no leaven shall be seen by you'). The leavened-loaf object is al-mukhammar (אלמכ'מר).
Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew אַרְבֶּה — the eighth plague (Exod 10:4-19); the destructive-pestilence-on-crops formulas (Deut 28:38, 42); the clean-insect list (Lev 11:22).

entries.gloss_en: ring, loop, link (especially of metal — the gold rings of the Tabernacle furnishings)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew טַבַּעַת in the Tabernacle-construction passages (Exod 25:12-15, 26-27; 26:24, 29; 27:4, 7; 28:23-28; 30:4; 35:22; 36:34; 37:3-5, 13-14, 27; 38:5, 7; 39:16-21). Plural ḥalaq, dual ḥalqatān.

entries.gloss_en: edge, border, margin (of a curtain, garment, page)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew שְׂפַת (in the construct 'edge of') in the Tabernacle-curtain passages (Exod 26:4, 10; 36:11, 17 — חאשיה' אלשקה 'the edge of the curtain').

Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew פֵּאָה in the Tabernacle-construction directional formulas (Exod 26:18, 20, 27, 35; 27:9, 11, 12, 13; 36:23, 25, 32 — מן גהה' מהב אלגנוב 'from the southern direction'; מן גהה' מהב אלשמאל 'from the northern direction').

entries.gloss_en: Hamor — Hivite chieftain of Shechem; father of Shechem the violator of Dinah (Gen 33:19; 34 passim; Josh 24:32; Judg 9:28)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged. The homograph with ḥamār 'donkey' is purely orthographic.

entries.gloss_en: Shechem — (1) son of Hamor the Hivite, violator of Dinah (Gen 33:19; 34); (2) the city in the central hill country between Mts. Gerizim and Ebal (Gen 12:6; 33:18; 37:12-14; Num 26:31; Josh 24:1, 32)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia retains the Hebrew name unchanged for both senses.
